# Modified HasteBoots proof implementation

The target is complete protocol 12, schedule 5, non-hiding Brakedown, Goldilocks
first and BabyBear second. Preserve native degree 1024, LWE dimension 728,
public evaluation keys and output keys. The final target is application
soundness/knowledge and 128-bit expected work per false acceptance in an
explicit classical ideal-oracle model. Encryption privacy and zero knowledge
are separate claims.

## Source success aggregates and capacity dispatch

The accepted layout branch now executes its original 16 aggregate, projection,
move and storage statements before the source zero-size switch. Lean proves
construction of `Layout { size: capacity, align: 1 }`, the two nominal `Ok`
wrappers and recovery of that layout into local 6. Temporary aggregate locals
are consumed and made dead in source order. The recovered size in local 7
selects the zero-size continuation exactly when the requested capacity is zero.

`layout_capacity_dispatch` composes this result with the earlier overflow and
layout-bound prefix for every capacity below `2^63`. The zero-size, positive-size,
rejected-layout, overflow and following continuations remain arbitrary; their
normal and exceptional outcomes are preserved. Source regressions exercise zero,
one and the largest accepted size, including a selected failing branch that
must suppress the following continuation. Fresh extraction validates both Result
success/error variant declarations, success field projections and the exact
unsigned zero-size switch. The unused reservation-error field type remains
arbitrary: this proves success-side operations without assigning a representation
to the source error type hidden by this extraction.

The fresh gate passes 361 dependency audits and 42 rejecting controls. Eight new
source regressions extend the earlier thirteen. No production interpreter module
or root import changed. The next source obligations are the zero-size return
construction and positive-size allocation-mode dispatch with its actual allocator
reference and call. Allocator/error execution, native ABI/compiler correspondence,
physical work and the final security theorem remain open.

## Continuous byte-allocation layout prefix

The retained `alloc::raw_vec::try_allocate_in` prefix now has an operational
Lean proof across its original 28 initial statements, overflow branch, nine
layout-check statements and consuming Boolean layout branch. For every 64-bit
capacity it computes byte size without multiplication overflow and selects the
valid layout suffix exactly when `capacity < 2^63`. The nominal `Layout`,
`Alignment`, all 64 alignment discriminants, physical field offsets and evaluated
byte-layout global are checked against fresh LLBC.

`layout_prefix_exact` is contextual: the overflow, valid-layout, invalid-layout
and following bodies are arbitrary. It preserves the following continuation on
normal completion and propagates other outcomes. The resulting frame preserves
the ambient world and unrelated locals, including both remaining arguments;
the moved layout-condition local contains an uninitialized value. This extends
the earlier isolated-assignment result to continuous source control flow.

The suffixes remain proof obligations. This result does not execute the source
allocator, build its success/error values, drop the allocator or establish a
native by-value ABI. Next, translate the valid-layout aggregate construction and
its allocation dispatch, then the actual error/abort suffixes, and compose them
with the existing modeled reservation/storage/destructor results. Compiler
refinement, physical attacker work and the final security theorem remain open.

## Retained allocation arithmetic and typed Boolean branches

The record interpreter now represents primitive Booleans separately from word
values. It evaluates checked multiplication with a result/overflow tuple, unsigned
comparisons, bit equality, wrapping and precondition-checked subtraction, wrapping
shift, bitwise OR and logical negation. Dynamic Boolean branches preserve the
actual operand move, execute only the selected branch and retain the following
continuation. Heap, incoming-reference and deallocation-budget proofs cover the
new cases. Wrong kinds and violated subtraction preconditions halt explicitly.

`interop/aeneas/vec-capacity-arithmetic` freshly extracts `Vec::<u8>::with_capacity`
and retains all 21 function declarations, 31 type declarations and globals. Nine
original arithmetic assignments are emitted with their exact destination/local
indices, declared primitive widths, operand modes and source statement hashes.
The checked multiplication assignment is proved for every 64-bit word pair and
modeled world, including the original two source moves. For byte element size one,
the unsigned multiplication result is exactly the requested capacity and its
overflow flag is false, even at the largest unsigned word. The continuous-prefix proof above additionally covers the later allocation
layout check.

The original isolated-assignment proofs use partial scalar contexts with unused
locals dead; the continuous-prefix proof above preserves arbitrary unrelated
locals. Whole constructor execution remains open. The complete retained Rust
control flow and calls are available for the next translation step; their success,
overflow/error handling, abort paths and native layout/ABI correspondence remain
unproved. No uninterpreted allocator success or error callback is introduced.

The extension adds 28 audited core declarations, five arithmetic theorems and two
world-preservation helper theorems. Enum dispatch now uses a stable named equation
in the destructor proofs. Seventeen model regressions cover overflow,
wrapping, rejected preconditions, kind/arity errors, genuine Boolean typing,
selected versus unsupported branches and consumption of a Boolean condition.
The new profile has 23 definitions, four source theorems and four source
regressions. Its gate checks 333 dependencies and 21 rejecting extraction controls
using the existing frozen toolchain. Full application security and physical-work
accounting remain open.

## Modeled fresh reservations retain buffer provenance through destruction

`NativePointerRestore` proves that writing back loaded initialized bytes preserves
the entire byte heap. A typed pointer store can then install the complete source
pointer's provenance without changing its address bytes. Integer-only header
writes still erase provenance, including when their bits are unchanged.

`NativeReservedVecStorage` writes arbitrary bounded capacity, the registered
buffer pointer and zero element length into a checked header. The actual byte
write, address derivation, typed store and fresh exclusive borrow produce the
resident descriptor and header frontier. Allocation identities and extents are
preserved. `NativeReservedVecConstruction.reserve_complete` adds a fresh modeled
allocation and derives ownership and full-capacity separation from explicit
allocator geometry, free space and loan separation. Successful allocation, writes,
borrows, initialized payload bytes and an already-owned result are not premises.

`modeled_reservation_destroy_complete` composes this model construction with the
retained reference-based Vec destructor. Every operational invocation returns
unit, preserves reachability, restores its complete ordered incoming loans and
frees exactly the stored original buffer and capacity. Spare payload bytes may
remain entirely uninitialized. The header's caller-owned loan remains live.

This adds 15 model theorems, five definitions, a readiness structure and two
source-composition theorems, with 24 declaration audits. Thirteen model regressions
cover fresh ownership, stored origins and generations, uninitialized payloads, exact extent,
integer-write erasure and typed restoration, overlapping storage, invalid header
extent, allocator overlap and the positive allocator's zero-size rejection. Two
source regressions cover canonical and arbitrary operational destruction.
The combined gate now audits 949 declarations and retains 87 extraction controls.

This is a fresh-allocation and storage theorem in the checked model. The original
Rust `with_capacity` body remains unproved, including its checked multiplication,
capacity assertion, allocation-error and abort paths. The existing empty profile
handles zero capacity; this model reservation primitive is positive-capacity.
Next connect the retained allocation-backed constructor to these model results
without dropping its failure paths. Compiler/native ABI and external allocator
correspondence, native by-value lifetime release, physical attacker work and final
application security remain open.

## Empty constructor to resident storage and reference destruction

`NativeEmptyVecStorage` proves a checked storage bridge for the original empty
byte Vec value. A registered pointer to a live 24-byte header, a reachable
modeled world, checked alignment/extent and separation from existing loans suffice
for the actual byte write and fresh exclusive borrow. Neither operation's success
is assumed. The resulting resident descriptor has capacity and length zero and
a dangling pointer with no allocation origin. Its initialization, buffer ownership,
empty buffer separation and exclusive header frontier are proved.

`HasteBootsVecEmpty.constructStored_complete` first invokes the retained original
constructor, validates its actual nominal fields, then performs that storage
sequence. The combined `empty_construct_destroy_complete` theorem feeds the
result directly into the retained complete reference-based Vec destructor.
`constructed_empty_every_invocation` gives the same normal unit return,
reachability, complete ordered incoming loans and unchanged stored heap to every
operational destructor invocation. This leaves the header's caller-owned loan
in place; native by-value drop and header lifetime discharge are not proved.

Seven model theorems, two definitions and a readiness structure have 11
declaration audits. Seven model regressions cover uninitialized header bytes,
actual descriptor construction, derived destructor conditions, unrelated live
loans, overlapping loans, misalignment and address bits without provenance.
The constructor profile now has seven source theorems, eight definitions and
six regressions. Two additional composition theorems and two regressions connect
the freshly extracted constructor and destructor profiles. The constructor gate
checks 304 dependencies and 17 rejection controls; the combined gate checks 925
dependencies and 87 controls. Both use the existing frozen toolchain.

This proves modeled serialization into the validated physical field layout.
Compiler/native ABI correspondence, positive-capacity constructors and ownership,
native lifetime/by-value release, the external allocator implementation, physical
attacker work and the final application security inequality remain open. Next
extend construction to the allocation-backed path, preserving capacity-overflow,
allocation-error and abort branches as well as success, while retaining these
explicit implementation-refinement boundaries.

## Initial nominal empty Vec constructor proof

The original byte `Vec::new` constructor and a direct caller are now freshly
extracted and checked in `interop/aeneas/vec-empty`. Six theorems prove their
exact nominal return value, zero capacity and length, unchanged incoming world,
and absence of allocation provenance on the dangling pointer. This holds for
arbitrary incoming modeled worlds. Even a live allocation at numerical address
one cannot make the returned pointer readable for a positive extent.

The interpreter gains a pure address literal; it creates no allocation, reference,
loan or allocation provenance. The reifier validates the original transmute,
evaluated byte alignment, all 64 physical alignment discriminants, nominal field
types and move/copy modes, constrained capacity and concrete layouts. Both
original function bodies and all ten type declarations are retained. The gate
checks 291 declaration dependencies, four regression examples and 17 rejecting
extraction controls using the existing frozen toolchain receipt.

This nominal result now supplies the checked resident storage bridge above.
Positive-capacity allocation, compiler/lifetime/ABI refinement, the external
allocator implementation, physical attacker work and the final application
security inequality remain open.

## Complete outer Vec destruction under resident model conditions

`VecDestructionProof.lean` composes the original outer destructor through the
whole-Vec borrow, original-length byte traversal, RawVec field borrow, proved
RawVec glue and final return. The first scope closes its temporary whole-Vec
loan before the RawVec borrow. The original descriptor is then re-indexed using
its retained reference and pointer identities; its fields and alias frontier
follow from the unchanged heap and exactly restored loan list.

`vec_glue_complete` proves normal unit return and reachability, with the original
ordered incoming loans restored. Zero capacity preserves the complete heap;
positive capacity frees exactly the original owned buffer and capacity layout.
Canonical invocation, every-invocation and deterministic-executor corollaries
retain those guarantees. Successful calls, cleanup results or a forced output
are not hypotheses.

The conditions are explicit: a descriptor bound to the stored fields, a reachable
modeled state, initialized element bytes, full-capacity separation from active
loans, an exclusive header frontier and ownership of the data allocation. The
native constructor and implementation refinements needed to establish these
conditions for actual Rust executions remain separate open obligations.

The native support adds four theorems and one descriptor-transport definition;
the source composition adds nine theorems and two checked definitions. All 16
declarations have dependency audits. Four model regressions cover both borrow
targets, descriptor re-indexing and preserved buffer separation. Four source
regressions cover three-byte destruction, an empty dangling buffer, a completely
uninitialized positive reservation with zero elements, and arbitrary operational
invocations. Original-extent completion proofs are checked alongside the
semantic guard that rejects replacing the element extent with zero.

Sufficient conditions for successful complete Vec destruction are now proved in
the checked model. Native construction/ownership acceptance, compiler/lifetime/
ABI refinement, the external allocator implementation, native physical-work
accounting and final application security remain open. The final 128-bit
expected-work inequality is not established by this destructor result.

The canonical invocation corollaries check the original input decoder. The

This step adds three model theorems and nine source theorems, with 12 declaration

## Register-bound references now use the provenance-aware heap

`NativeReferenceMachine` binds reference operations to reference registers.
Operands select registers rather than supplying ledger tags or reference
records. Checked root borrows and reborrows mint the reference values and record
their birth leases. The ledger is a view of the existing pointer-machine heap,
so byte memory is shared rather than duplicated. Raw pointer reads, writes,
copies and frees check ledger permissions; allocation and pointer-value
construction retain their existing checked semantics.

Tagged accesses select a resident lease, check its mode and bounds, derive the
access pointer with the lease's allocation origin, and check the ledger's
through-access permissions. Byte reads/writes and pointer loads/stores use the
concrete heap and origin metadata. Pointer stores retain data origins; numerical
writes erase them. Scratch-register recovery selects an existing complete
pointer value, never a provenance reconstructed from address bits. Every
resident lease retains its original pointer in the registers, and recovery is
proved available for that pointer.

Forty-one theorems cover exact reference/lease/pointer binding, projection into
the closed pointer machine, heap/ledger well-formedness, causal checked-borrow
birth witnesses, unique minted tags, monotone counters, raw-free conflict
exclusion and permanent revocation. After a reference ends, every later access
selecting that old tag is rejected, even after new borrows. The strongest birth
result starts from a successful program run on the concrete empty state and
exposes the earlier actual checked borrow and an execution suffix reaching the
current state. The pointer-machine projection preserves allocation-origin
authenticity through reference operations.

Persistent dependency audits cover 88 declarations, including record fields,
operation constructors and execution/effect constructors. Thirty-six executable
regressions exercise shared/exclusive access, parent/child overlap and disjoint
access, byte framing, pointer round trips, metadata erasure, raw conflicts,
layout/bounds/alignment checks, stale references, no tag reuse, and free blocked
by overlapping borrows. The model and tests are included in the root
aggregates. Full `scripts/check` passes (10,963 build jobs plus all subsequent
audit/smoke commands; log: `/tmp/hasteboots-reference-machine-full-check.log`).
Production Rust and the compiler/backend are unchanged.

This is a closed reference-binding and ledger-policy result. Complete Rust
alias/provenance semantics, multi-actor authority, references stored in heap
fields and original-source lifetime instrumentation remain open. The scratch
registers and ledger checks have no physical-cost interpretation here. Next,
connect the checked pointer/reference operations to the original native
pointer/lifecycle and typed source bodies. Native constructor extraction,
compiler/caller/NTT/SIMD/scheduler coverage, causal lifetime oracle-owner history,
BabyBear and the final expected physical attacker-work inequality remain open.
No end-to-end security theorem is claimed.

## Closed pointer programs now have causal allocation-origin authenticity

`NativePointerMachine` restricts pointer construction to nine data-only
operations: checked allocation, construction from numerical addresses, address
replacement on a selected register, pointer load/store, byte writes, copying,
nonoverlapping copying and free. Operands contain addresses, byte payloads,
layouts and register indices, with no pointer records or allocation identities.
Numerical construction supplies no origin; address replacement preserves the
selected register's origin. The machine has no operation for importing a
caller-supplied origin. Allocation records its checked base/layout and the
allocator's actual generation.

Thirty-five theorems establish heap well-formedness, register/stored-value
origin authenticity and generation bounds through every operation and arbitrary
finite executions. Every history entry has an actual successful allocator step
and an execution suffix reaching the current state. The strongest program
results start from the concrete empty state and expose the underlying successful
byte-heap allocator result for each register or stored pointer origin, with that
causal suffix. These do not assume the authenticity invariant as input.
Allocation generations in reachable histories are pairwise distinct, and the
next allocation generation has not already been issued. Historical origins
remain authentic after free; storage checks still reject stale dereferences.

Persistent dependency audits cover 71 declarations, including operation and
execution constructors and record fields. Twenty-four executable regressions
exercise all nine operations, numerical forgery attempts, origin-preserving
address changes, wrong-allocation accesses, initialized/uninitialized copying,
overlap policy, missing registers, overlapping allocation, exact free layouts,
double free, stale access after address reuse and retained dangling values.
The model and tests are included in the root aggregates. Full `scripts/check`
passes (10,960 build jobs plus all subsequent audit/smoke commands; log:
`/tmp/hasteboots-pointer-machine-full-check.log`). Production Rust and the
compiler/backend are unchanged.

This is allocation-origin authenticity for this closed memory machine. It does

## Thin pointer bytes and allocation origins now compose

`NativePointerByteMemory` couples the concrete byte heap to finite per-byte
allocation-origin metadata. Thin pointers occupy eight initialized little-endian
bytes with alignment eight; the stored address comes from those bytes and the
origin comes from a uniform metadata span. Null and dangling pointer values can
be stored without dereferencing their targets. Mixed-origin spans are rejected
by this explicit model policy. This is not a general Rust typed-layout or alias
semantics theorem.

Thirty-one theorems establish pointer store/load and copy/load round trips,
checked store availability, heap well-formedness, exact metadata changes on
allocation/free, and stale storage load/store rejection. Copies snapshot both
bytes and metadata before writing, including overlap. Numerical word writes
clear origins even when the stored address bits remain unchanged. Freeing an
allocation removes metadata owned by its storage while retaining dangling
pointer values in other allocations. Load origins must come from existing
metadata cells; copies and numerical writes cannot introduce new origins, and
pointer stores can introduce only the supplied value's origin.

All 44 declarations have persistent dependency audits. Nineteen executable
regressions cover uninitialized storage, actual address bytes, numeric origin
erasure, partial fragments, alignment, overlapping relocation, uninitialized
copies, null values, dangling values, address reuse and storage cleanup. The
model and tests are included in the root aggregates. Full `scripts/check` passes
(10,957 build jobs plus all subsequent audit/smoke commands; log:
`/tmp/hasteboots-pointer-byte-memory-full-check.log`). Production Rust and the
compiler/backend are unchanged.

The subsequent closed machine above proves allocation-origin authenticity
for its register and stored pointer values. The low-level storage API still
accepts supplied pointer values and does not itself authenticate them. Connecting these operations to original native
pointer accesses and lifecycle bodies, borrow identity, compiler/caller/NTT/
SIMD/scheduler coverage, causal lifetime oracle-owner history, BabyBear and the
final expected physical attacker-work inequality all remain open. This is not a
native constructor acceptance or an end-to-end security result.

## Untyped byte copies and finite allocation-origin metadata now check

`NativeRawByteRange` snapshots and replaces actual heap cells, including
uninitialized cells. Positive copies snapshot before writing, so overlapping
copies retain the original source cells. A separate nonoverlapping operation
rejects overlapping spans. Empty copies check alignment without dereferencing
storage. Thirty-one theorems establish exact read-back, initialization-state
preservation, agreement with initialized byte writes, outside-byte framing,
well-formedness and derived availability from checked spans. These are model
operations; native pointer-copy source correspondence and physical costs remain
open. Rust's [copy_nonoverlapping documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/core/ptr/fn.copy_nonoverlapping.html)
specifies untyped copying that preserves initialization state, motivating the
cell representation rather than an initialized-values-only copy.

`NativePointerShadow` provides finite per-byte allocation-origin metadata keyed
by the containing allocation's identity and byte address. Replacement and
snapshot operations support relocation. Integer-byte writes can clear metadata
even when address bits stay unchanged. Eleven theorems establish selected-cell
membership, exact inside replacement, outside framing, snapshot length and
uniform-span behavior. Mixed fragments are rejected by this model's policy;
this does not establish the complete Rust provenance or aliasing rules. The
standalone metadata layer does not authenticate caller-supplied pointers; the
heap composition is described above. No allocation origin is reconstructed
by searching live allocations for matching address bits. Rust's
[without_provenance documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/core/ptr/fn.without_provenance.html)
explains why numerical addresses alone cannot authorize nonzero memory access.

All 61 new declarations, including the metadata record's constructor and
projections, have persistent dependency audits limited to the three permitted
Lean dependencies. Eighteen executable regressions cover uninitialized and
overlapping copies, nonoverlap and extent rejection, stale allocation
identities, zero-length alignment, partial metadata erasure, generation-separated
storage and metadata relocation. Both modules and their tests are included in
the root aggregates. Full `scripts/check` passes (10,954 build jobs plus all
subsequent audit/smoke commands; log:
`/tmp/hasteboots-raw-byte-shadow-full-check.log`). Production Rust and the
compiler/backend are unchanged.

The subsequent composition above supplies pointer load/store/copy round trips
and lifecycle behavior. Closing pointer-value construction under source

security theorem is claimed by these modules.

## Local mutable reborrow call and checked scope restoration now check

The original safe Rust fixture now takes a local mutable cell reborrow and
passes it to a read/replace helper. Both original bodies, signature lifetimes,
mutable index/helper call and the mutable/two-phase reference rvalues are
retained. The complete generated continuation passes the helper's updated cell
back to the parent slice. Four source theorems prove all-input behavior.

`NativeByteReborrow.replaceAt` computes a closed local child scope using the
existing checked ledger: resolve/bounds-check the parent, acquire the selected
child, read/write its byte, then end it. Thirteen model theorems establish exact
execution, heap updates, well-formedness, original caller lease restoration and
permanent child revocation. A checked initial grant derives the child's read
and write permissions and successful completion/release. No arbitrary callee
callback, claimed old value or release certificate replaces these operations.
Three source/heap bridge theorems connect the old byte, updated source slice and
resulting current heap, including the unchanged out-of-bounds branch.

## Shared/exclusive byte access and reborrow lifetimes now check

`NativeByteBorrow` routes accesses through a checked byte-borrow ledger.
Acquisition checks initialized geometry and conflicts. Reborrows require a
resident parent, contained span and unchanged origin, and cannot upgrade shared
to exclusive access. Accesses through a tag may exempt real ancestors, while
unrelated conflicts reject. Disjoint child ranges and parent accesses outside
a child range are supported.

Fifty-four model theorems establish checked access, actual byte writes and
allocation removal, parent residency/bounds/modes, unique tags and preserved
memory/ledger invariants. The ancestry checker is sound and complete for valid
resident tags, and parent paths strictly decrease. Ending a parent waits for
children; an ended tag never reappears under any future model transition.
Seven composition theorems connect original byte-slice pointer constructors to
the same checked pointer/origin/length and initialization conditions.

writes, nested/disjoint reborrows, revocation and empty ranges. The compiler,

## Initialized byte ranges now share source pointer data

The byte-memory model now supports checked byte ranges and byte-slice views.
Positive reads must stay inside one live allocation with matching origin, and
every requested byte must be initialized. The result has the exact requested
length. Addresses are nonnull/aligned and `address + size < 2^64` is checked with
natural-number arithmetic before address conversion. Adjacent allocations cannot
be joined into a slice. Empty ranges retain the nonnull/aligned requirement but
do not require a live allocation; typed ZST multiplicity and Rust borrow validity
remain separate obligations.

Twenty-four model theorems establish coverage, initialization, exact lengths,
nonwrapping arithmetic, empty cases, deallocated-alias rejection and agreement
with single-byte loads. An initialized covering block in a well-formed state
also derives successful range execution. Nine bridge theorems connect original
constant/mutable/cast byte-slice pointer constructors to the same address,
provenance and length used in these checks. This is pointer-data composition,
not an accepted Rust dereference or a borrow permission.

## Checked byte allocation lifecycle and source Layout bridge

The shared pointer data now supports an explicit byte-memory model. Allocation
checks layout, nonzero/aligned base, address-space extent and disjoint live
ranges; it generates a fresh origin and uninitialized byte slots. Loads require
an initialized byte in the matching live allocation. Stores update that byte.
Deallocation requires the original base/origin and exact layout and removes the
allocation and its bytes. Every successful release reduces the live-block count.
Zero-size allocator calls are rejected; source ZST/empty paths remain separate.

Thirty-nine theorems prove operation/heap invariants, read-after-write,
initialized/in-bounds access witnesses, framing, deallocated-alias rejection and
stale address-reuse behavior. Reachability derives well-formedness from the empty
heap. The proof-only shape erasure does not replace any memory/destructor action.
Six bridge theorems link the extracted stdlib Layout getters to model inputs,
all alignment constructors and the checked allocation/deallocation conditions.
The source Layout gate is rerun in its existing configuration; this does not
establish configuration identity or a native source allocator simulation.

## Heap simulation preserves complete registry failure

Four additional `Heap.lean` theorems establish agreement on read failure and
on complete registry failure. Ordered materialization fails exactly when some
original borrow is unreadable, including unused and duplicate references.
Under the whole-heap representation, this agrees with resolution failure and
with failure of the full pointer-backed registry; represented cells cannot
resolve to invalid arena handles. This complements the existing successful
materialization and extraction composition.

These statements describe the operational model, not runtime invalid-reference
detection in Rust. Establishing valid Rust references, allocator/source
refinement, actual failure costs and the complete security theorem remains
open. No native verifier checks were introduced.

## Whole-heap simulation derives registry compatibility

`Heap.lean` relates native parameter-value cells to retained arena handles over
the entire heap, independently of registry borrows. The relation preserves
address and allocation identity and decodes each native value to its arena
entry. Empty heaps, arena extension, paired retention and paired retirement
preserve it. Successful reads and ordered carrier materialization then derive
both compatible registry results, including original roots and duplicate
borrows. Ownership and observed-extraction wrappers use this derived pointer
registry result instead of requesting an independent compatibility run.

This is an immutable operational heap simulation. The global representation
and native carrier materialization still need to be derived from actual Rust
allocation/borrowing/source execution. Allocation freshness, object layout,
context bytes, actor-separated physical work and complete security remain
open; no native verifier checks or runtime proof certificates were added.

copy are charged. `StoredGoldCodeEncodingCost` serializes all retained code fields
in original order, including padded message blocks, raw modulus bytes and raw
domain root. Its value equals `NativeGoldBlockCode.codec.encode`, costs at most
`6*codeModulusBytes+600`, and produces at most `codeModulusBytes+54` bytes.

`StoredGoldContextEncodingCost` now encodes the **complete original parameter
context hash input** from retained fields. The outer modulus, all six native
parameter/accessor words, row-code domain and complete retained code object are
included without a caller serializer. Its value equals
`NativeBrakedownContext.input NativeGoldBlockCode.description.row`, and structural
injectivity is inherited from the complete native context codec. Encoding is
linear in retained modulus bytes with explicit fixed-domain bounds. Raw field
representatives remain unchanged; no code-root validity or hash-collision claim
is inferred from serialization alone.

`StoredGoldContextObservationCost` now verifies that exact complete context bytes
and an exact 64-byte stored context appear in an actual hash observation. Starts,
SHAKE outputs, different input bytes and truncated/trailing hash responses cannot
stand in for that observation. Encoding, full byte comparisons and history scan
are charged. Under truthful history, acceptance identifies the native SHA-512
context and the exact native context-program result/log. Conversely, an included
native context execution returning that digest produces acceptance. Two verified
parameter objects for the same context are equal outside the **existing shared
hash-cache collision event**, using complete-input injectivity; no independent
hash event, collision certificate or oracle callback is added to execution.

`ObservedGoldFieldExtraction` now requires the parsed field count to equal the
validated geometry's actual shared random count, and verifies its complete
parameter-context association before extracting from the original recovered
snapshot. Its success theorem derives those checks; its operation bound includes
the entire prior extraction path, complete context encoding and history scan.
An accepted parameter object is proved equal to an original object's included
native context initializer outside that same shared-cache collision event.
The original application-orchestration gap at this layer is addressed by
`StoredGoldRegistryAssociation` above, conditional on the actual registry-packet
and selected-field-key links; full application and physical refinement remain open.

Eleven regression groups and thirty-three theorem axiom guards cover raw byte

`StoredGeometryArithmeticCost` now supplies explicit charged power-of-two and

`StoredGoldGeometryCost` now validates the retained Gold parameter object with

`NativeBrakedownParameters.build NativeGoldBlockCode.description` on every
parameter input. The original basic, code-shape and allocation gates are
preserved; invalid large exponents reject before the power loops. Constructor

cost is at most `1500`, using the existing native 64-bit input bounds. Scalar
word/physical/backend refinement is not implied by that operation count.

`ValidatedGoldFieldExtraction` now produces the extractor's capacity witness at
runtime. It first runs the measured native geometry gate, then checks the
preceding extractor's explicit message-capacity precondition. This additional
extractor gate is stated in its value theorem; it is not silently added to the
original native geometry constructor. `constructor_complete` reuses the existing
`NativeGoldBlockCodeMeaning.constructor_dimensions` theorem to prove every
successful native code constructor with accepted geometry passes it. Validation
costs at most `1516`; rejected dimensions stop before field parsing, causal replay
or extraction. The extraction entry point takes no separate capacity certificate
and includes validation plus the complete earlier extraction bound.

`StoredRegistryOwnerCost` now performs charged index access and first-original
full-key lookup in all stored registry slots. The returned index equals
`NativeSourceRegistry.owner` exactly. Earlier unused aliases participate,
different complete contexts sharing a root remain distinct, and differing roots
remain distinct. There is no used-slot filtering or registry reordering. Lookup
costs at most `1329*registryLength+6`, including access to the queried key.

Ten regression groups and twenty-seven theorem axiom guards cover arithmetic
word boundaries, computed geometry/random count, early large-exponent/basic

`FrameMatchCost` now prices complete frame kind/label/message equality and

`StoredGoldBatchFieldInputCost` now decodes the **complete original raw field

reversal, exact suffix checks and complete batch payload decoding.

`StoredGoldFieldSourceRecovery` now produces the source key from that parsed

The caller supplies raw stream bytes and mixed history, not a key, source log

`StoredGoldFieldExtraction` composes this raw-input parser/recovery with measured

composition does not establish application parameter validity or ownership.

Ten regression groups and twenty-five theorem axiom guards cover exact integer

`CausalPrefixReadCost` now recovers the complete mixed-history prefix before a
stream's first positive read using charged byte comparisons and list traversal.
Starts, hashes and empty reads remain in the prefix; they do not count as
exposure. Any offset counts, including far-offset and earlier partial reads.
The output equals `CausalFirstStreamPrefix.recover` on every input/history.
Recovery costs at most `(6*streamBytes+16)*P+1` and is stable under later history
extensions once a boundary exists. No oracle or functional cache callback runs.

`CausalStoredSourceRecovery` now composes that original boundary with stored
snapshot replay and selection. Even missing-key fallback uses the current log of
the **recovered prefix**, never the later full history. The viewed result equals
the original executable source recovery when the supplied stream/key correspond
to a native field view; source stability under appended observations is proved.
The all-history entry point includes the complete recovery and replay charges,
with a polynomial bound in actual history input/output bytes, observation count
and target stream bytes. Prefix-size inequalities and budget monotonicity are
derived, without a lifetime or seed-window cap.

`CausalStoredGoldExtraction` now feeds the causally recovered stored log and
stored root bytes directly into the measured Gold Merkle/column/code extractor.
Its result equals the original public-source extractor on the original selected

callback is executed. The trusted typed context, radius and capacity proof are
still supplied as in the preceding extractor interface; producing/validating them
from the original application instance is not discharged by this composition.

`StoredHashLogCost` now retains all ordered hash observations as stored bytes,
including unrelated/off-path inputs and repeated entries. Its fixed-size measured
decoder exactly matches `JointHashCache.decode` on arbitrary analysis histories:
missing bytes are zero-padded and bytes beyond 64 are ignored. Decoding costs at

existing analysis decoder, not acceptance of malformed native SHA-512 outputs.
Strict native output parsing/refinement remains a separate obligation.

`StoredSourceSnapshotHistory` now replays immutable stored source snapshots.
Each first-frozen full context/root key stores one mark sharing the exact current
immutable hash log. Later hashes append to the current log and cannot alter old
marks. The 64-height expansion exists only in the semantic view, which equals
`CompactSourceHistory.reconstruct` exactly, including the full ordered checkpoint
list and its common logs. Stored snapshot keys equal the stored frozen list,
so marks are unique and their count is at most `4*N^2`. Current hash count is at
most observation count `P`. Complete hash observations, partial seeds, inherited
metadata, aliases and all freeze roles retain their existing causal semantics.

`StoredSourceSnapshotBudget` proves a polynomial operation bound for complete
ledger/cache/hash/snapshot replay. With total observed input bytes `N`, observation
count `P` and observed output bytes `Q`, replay costs at most
`stepBound N P Q * P + 1`. Mark construction charges record/pointer construction
and list appends; fixed digest decoding and hash-log append traversals are charged
separately. Physical memory/compiler/backend refinement is not inferred from
persistent sharing in this reference program.

`StoredSourceSnapshotSelection` now performs charged full context/root byte
lookup in the stored marks. Coverage and uniqueness are derived from replay.
The selected stored-log view is proved equal to the original
`ExecutableSourceSelection.select (ExecutableSourceHistory.reconstruct history)`
for every history and stored key. The proof covers every height and the original
candidate-log search, including real empty-log snapshots and missing-key current-log
fallback. Keys sharing only a root do not merge. Lookup costs at most
`5308*N^2+3`; the complete-history entry point includes replay cost as well.
No functional digest/cache/selection callback executes in that entry point.

`StoredFrozenRequestsCost` now executes complete source-request preparation
using stored context/root pairs. It resolves every compatible parent against the
current cache, applies the original compact-request deduplication, filters keys

in exact order; the resulting frozen view equals its `next.frozen`. Different
contexts sharing a root remain distinct. Every comparison, compaction, filter and

`StoredFrozenLedgerHistory` now replays the **full parent ledger, frozen-key set
and SHAKE byte cache** of `CompactParentHistory`. It emits the exact fresh request
list at each nonempty-output transition. Starts, hashes and empty outputs still
discover metadata but emit no requests and freeze no keys. Nonempty outputs use

observed bytes. Repeated outputs and later corrections cannot refreeze a key.
The stored frozen list is proved unique and has length at most `4*N^2`, where `N`
is total actual observed input bytes. Earlier complete but unused source aliases
are included in the freeze requests; this is not yet the application registry's
first-original-owner theorem.

`StoredFrozenLedgerBudget` derives an explicit polynomial operation bound for
that entire ledger replay, including extra source resolution, deduplication and

The bound is obtained from actual metadata/cache/frozen-list invariants, without

`StoredMetadataCost` now supplies closed byte-vector equality, source-pair
equality, list membership and compact-ledger last-occurrence deduplication.
Comparisons inspect stored bytes, with no functional digest callback. Root/source
equality costs at most `660`/`1323`; membership costs at most `664*L+1`/
`1327*L+1`; deduplication costs at most `668*(L+1)^2`/`1331*(L+1)^2`.
Generic loops include every supplied comparison charge; public root/source
endpoints fix concrete byte programs. Their views match the existing compact
ledger's deduplication, independently of registry ownership and snapshot order.

`StoredParentContributionsCost`, `StoredParentResolutionCost`,
`StoredBindingHelpersCost` and `StoredParentContextsCost` now compose all stored
parent-source/helper contributions. They retain every compatible parent record,

`StoredParentMetadataHistory` now replays the **complete inherited parent metadata
and byte-cache projection** of `CompactParentHistory` and `CompactSourceHistory`.
Every start, hash and output observation is visited, including empty outputs.
Metadata is resolved using the preceding cache and compacted before the current
output bytes are written. Later exposures cannot retrospectively change stored
parent metadata. Hash answers are not SHAKE exposures; all observed SHAKE bytes
remain in the cache, including repeated/overlapping writes. Exact parent-record
and cache-view equivalences are proved for every history, without a lifetime or
trial cap. The stored state deliberately projects parent metadata and byte cache;
it does not yet execute frozen-request or snapshot transitions.

`StoredParentMetadataBudget` derives polynomial replay time from the existing
compact metadata invariant. For total actual input bytes `N`, observation count
`P` and actual observed output bytes `Q`, both source and helper entry counts are
bounded by `M = P*(4*N^2+2*N)`. Stored parent-input bytes are at most `N`, parent
records at most `P`, and cached entries exactly `Q`. Its explicit polynomial
`stepBound N P Q` bounds each metadata step. Complete replay costs at most
`(stepBound N P Q+8*Q+8)*P+1`. These parameters bound extractor operations;
no observation-count fee is granted to the attacker.

`StoredHistorySourceResolutionCost.run` uses that causal stored replay for a new
raw child input. Its source view equals the complete compact-history resolver,
with an explicit polynomial time bound and output length at most
`childBytes + M*(childBytes+1)`. It does not recompute old metadata using the final
cache. This closes the previously open stored source/helper inheritance path.

Nine regression groups cover full-byte comparisons, distinct contexts sharing a

`GoldBatchQueriesCost` now measures the outer original batch-query vector,
including every nested matrix reader/encoder. Its prefix decoder equals the
original vector codec on every input, costs at most `145*(N+1)+3`, and successful
reads cost at most `145*consumed+1`. For outer query weight `W` (the sum of query
weights plus one per query), serialization costs at most `379*W+93` and produces
at most `9*(W+1)` bytes.

`StoredBatchMessageCost` reads the original context/root pair, complete ordered
query vector and complete nested response table. Raw words, empty/ragged rows,
empty queries and mismatched query/value counts are retained for subsequent
semantic verification. Strict decoding charges EOF checking, full canonical
re-encoding and byte comparison. All-input equality to the original exact batch
codec, accepted-byte reconstruction, view injectivity and stored round trips are
proved. Decoding costs at most `557*N+2400`; a context/root prefix alone cannot
supply a source when the remaining payload is malformed or noncanonical.
`StoredBatchFramesCost` checks original batch kind/label roles and projects its
stored pair exactly to the original frame-source branch.

`StoredSourceMentionsCost` now composes **all original direct source formats**:
registry vectors, canonical bindings, complete batch messages and adjacent
single openings. Its output, viewed as native context/root pairs, equals
`NativeRootInputView.mentions` and, from raw bytes, `ExecutableParentLedger.direct`.
It retains original order, duplicates and distinct contexts sharing a root:
frame sources first, the actual adjacent single pair next, then remaining frames.
Malformed payloads contribute no source; malformed outer framing rejects the
whole stream. With `Kr`, `Kb`, `Km` the three source labels and `Kc`, `Ko` the
single-opening labels' byte lengths, the closed raw-input operation bound is
`(9456+12*(Kr+Kb+Km)+6*(Kc+Ko))*N+5`. Output length is at most `N`.
These are explicit reference byte/list/word operation bounds, not physical
runtime measurements or attacker-work credit.

`VectorWireReadCost` and `VectorWireEncodeCost` now provide measured repeated

`GoldQueryWireCost` instantiates those loops for original width/value matrices,

`StoredSingleOpeningCost` now measures complete root/query/response decoding,

`StoredSingleSourcesCost` checks the original adjacent context/opening frame

source view. All charges are reference byte/list/word upper bounds, not physical

`StoredBindingFramesCost` charges exact binding kind/label checks, complete message

`StoredSourceVectorReadCost` now measures native context/root source-vector

`StoredSourceVectorCost` adds measured canonical serialization and strict complete

full serialization at most `848*R+93`. Strict decoding equals the original exact

every canonical stored vector. Its bound is `1764*(N/128+1)+6*N+1`. Different
contexts sharing a root remain distinct; original duplicate pairs remain present.
No functional context/root or serializer callback executes in these programs.

`StoredRegistrySourcesCost` measures the registry-frame branch of original source

copying and full outer-frame parsing. Its viewed result equals the guarded
registry projection of `NativeRootInputView.frameSources`. For fixed registry
label length `K`, collection from `N` raw bytes costs at most `(3624+6*K)*N+5`.
Invalid registry payloads contribute no pairs; malformed outer framing rejects
the whole stream. This component does not replace the other source-mention
formats: canonical bindings, adjacent single openings and batched messages remain
separate measured-decoder obligations. No first-owner selection or deduplication
is introduced. First original complete context/root registry ownership, including
earlier unused aliases, remains a full-execution obligation.

Eleven regressions and thirty-seven axiom guards cover forged counts, suffixes,
shared roots under distinct contexts, duplicates, context/root byte fidelity,
noncanonical count headers, truncated pairs, rejection work, exact registry
labels, mixed payloads, whole-stream rejection and exact charges.

These are
reference byte/list/access upper bounds, not physical runtime or attacker-work

`StoredDigestVectorReadCost` now measures native digest-vector prefix reading
into stored 64-byte vectors. A successful digest consumes exactly 64 supplied
bytes; a forged count stops at the first truncated digest. The body bound is
`457*(min(count,N/64)+1)`, and the full prefix-reader bound is
`457*(N/64+1)+110`. Pure structural length proofs provide the bounded-vector
witness independently of arithmetic resource bounds. Prefix value equality to
the existing native codec holds for every input and preserves arbitrary suffixes.

`StoredDigestVectorCost` adds charged serialization and strict complete canonical
decoding. Body serialization costs exactly `327*R+1` for `R` stored roots; full
serialization costs at most `330*R+93`. The strict decoder matches
`NativeExactCodec.read (vector digest)` on every input, reconstructs the supplied
bytes on success, and round-trips every canonical stored vector. Its bound is
`787*(N/64+1)+6*N+1`. Alternate/noncanonical count spellings, truncation and
trailing bytes reject. All raw digest bytes, root order and duplicates survive.
No digest or serializer callback executes in these producers/readers.

`StoredHelperRootsCost` measures helper-root recognition and collection from
complete native framed inputs. Kind/label checks, vector decoding/canonicality,

viewed as digests, equals `ExecutableParentLedger.roots` for every raw input.
With fixed helper-root label length `K`, the raw-input upper bound is
`(1644+6*K)*N+5`. These are reference byte/list/access upper bounds, not physical
runtime or attacker-work credit.

Eleven regressions and twenty-nine axiom guards cover huge declared counts,

`ParentSeedRequestCost` now measures the original terminal parent seed-request
recognizer. It parses the whole frame stream, reverses the stored frames and

This recognizes the existing structural view; ownership and trusted parameter

`ParentInputHistoryCost` discovers all parent inputs from complete mixed
histories. Starts, hashes and every output (including empty outputs) are visited.
The resulting newest-first list exactly equals the original compact ledger's

input bytes are `I` and observation count is `H`, replay costs at most
`27*I+A*H+1`, with `A = 6*Kp+6*M+37`. It stores at most `H` parent entries with
total shared input byte length at most `I`. Source/helper metadata is not created
by this projection and is not assumed free.

`HistoryParentCandidatesCost.run` now computes parent-input candidates directly
from the complete raw history and child input, without a caller-supplied parent
ledger. It composes measured parent discovery, stored SHAKE-coordinate replay,

Its result equals the active-parent input projection of the full compact ledger,
for every history and child input. Unknown seed coordinates remain wildcards;
only observed conflicts reject, and original duplicates/order are preserved.
With output bytes `B`, child-input bytes `N` and fixed child-seed label length
`Kc`, its upper bound is
`27*I+8*B+(A+459)*H+24*N+6*Kc+497+64*(6*I+14*H)*B`.
Invalid child inputs return no candidates while retaining all replay/parse cost.
These are abstract byte/list/access upper bounds, not attacker-work credit or

`SizedFrameCost`, `TranscriptFrameCost` and `TranscriptFrameStreamCost` now

prepared log, absent and partial branches, malformed-first aliases, cyclic dummy

BabyBear arithmetic executes in the generic extraction regression; native
BabyBear verification and its complete work-security theorem remain open.
No full PBS application-security theorem is claimed.

Native batch-model accepted-false-analysis-claim coverage now uses the closed
interpreter's actual instruction clock. `ClosedByteMachineLineage` supplies the
exact first positive-read packet and complete chronological log split, including
all earlier prequeries and silent instructions. `ClosedByteMachineNativeCoverage`
ports the native near/far accepted-run reduction onto those packets and derives
the trusted quota/coefficient filter from native preparation. No first-read,
freshness, source-log or eligibility certificate is added to verification.

`ClosedByteMachineNativeSoundness` transports arbitrary accepted batch witnesses
with varying roots, parents, responses and schedulers under the same public
parameters/profile into the priced hazard union. Its failure event is measurable
for arbitrary scheduler memory types, using replay of the actual native witness
on complete attainable histories. The lifetime theorem gives
`Pr[any native accepted false analysis claim] ≤ rate * expectedWork`; the
calibrated form gives
`2^128 * Pr[failure] ≤ (9/4096) * expectedWork` in declared interpreter units.
The original-size Goldilocks role premises still require successful code
construction, the primitive-root premise and compatible trusted parameters
including `Q ≥ 544`.

Validation for the earlier native-coverage milestone: `scripts/check` passed all 10,612 build jobs and its strict
audit/smoke commands. Six focused strict closed-native, root-work and earlier
native-lifetime checks passed. Eight new guards use only `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Regression checks cover the exact priced
packet lineage across silent instructions, witness-event measurability,
hazard coverage and the constructor-backed scaled lifetime interface. The
numerical fixture does not assert a complete PBS run. Native defaults and
proof limits are unchanged.

The earlier theorem uses the common-source analysis extractor; the executable
counterpart above proves equivalence at the native batch interface. The event
retains actual Lean native-program acceptance/log inclusion, canonical parsed
views and framing/capacity premises. Neither strict Rust execution refinement
nor public PBS semantics is inferred from those premises. Remaining work includes
public evaluator/extractor implementation and cost refinement, original registry/context
ownership (including unused aliases and parent/seed hazards at that boundary),
honest/verifier actor-cost and submission-cost separation, randomized setup,
physical pricing, BabyBear execution and strict decoder/NTT/SIMD/Div64/scheduler
refinement. A full modified-PBS application security theorem remains open.

The global source/collision event now has an unbounded first-moment work
bound for the closed byte interpreter. `NativeRootFamilyHashStep` combines the
existing posterior checkpoint and cached-hash collision laws under the complete
mixed history. Prior bad states are retained explicitly. Starts and SHAKE reads
preserve the bad-state predicate, and cached hash calls have zero fresh charge.
`ClosedByteMachineRootFailure` derives the conditional and averaged first-new-
failure laws and locates every actual global bad prefix at an earlier actual
hash instruction. No one-observation/one-instruction clock assumption is used.

`ClosedByteMachineRootWork` uses the derived per-hash envelope and an
analysis-only work split. Low-work charges sum against actual instruction
prices; Markov pays the entire large-work branch. With analysis threshold
`2^160`, the global root/source/collision lifetime probability is at most
`2^-159 * expectedWork`. The execution is unrestricted, infinite means are
allowed, and no finite second moment or success floor is assumed.

`ClosedByteMachineGoldAllRisk` unites that global event with the existing
field/column/receipt events on the SAME interpreter execution and proves
measurability and the unconditioned bound
`(2^-159 + 17/2^141 + 2^-255) * expectedWork`. Its coefficient is at most
`18/2^141`. The numerical allowance satisfies
`2^128 * (64 * 4 * coefficient) ≤ 9/16`. This last inequality is arithmetic;
it does not prove how the application consumes a shape/role union, and the
finite factors are not attacker trial or lifetime caps.

Validation: `scripts/check` passed all 10,608 build jobs and its strict
audit/smoke commands. Six focused strict root-work, root-budget and receipt-work
checks passed. Twenty-five new guards use only `propext`, `Classical.choice`
and `Quot.sound`. Tests include cached-query zero charge, non-hash preservation,
a concrete truthful collision world with earlier instruction coverage, stopped
zero charge, the numerical work split, and the combined constructor-backed
Goldilocks event bound. Native defaults and proof limits are unchanged.

The priced union now covers native-model false analysis claims on the closed
instruction clock as described above. Public PBS application coverage still
requires independent public evaluation and efficient extraction. Honest/verifier actor costs, initialization and submission
cost separation, randomized initialization, original registry/context ownership,
physical-unit refinement, BabyBear execution and strict Rust/decoder/NTT/SIMD/
Div64/scheduler refinement remain required. These interpreter-unit bounds do
not yet establish the full 128-bit modified-PBS application theorem.

The actual root/source registry now has a derived per-hash work envelope.
`NativeRootFamilyBudget` proves that the reconstructed history records exactly
64 shape checkpoints per distinct frozen context/root key. Request uniqueness
and the exact frozen-cardinality increment follow from the actual ledger's
`eraseDups` and fresh-key filter. The existing node-budget clamp bounds a fresh
hash's combined source/collision charge by
`(3 * populatedHashKeys + recordedCheckpoints) / 2^512`; no full-tree-size
factor is needed.

`NativeParentLedgerPools` proves every frozen source belongs to the Cartesian
product of context and root values found in actual observed inputs. All
compatible parents, partial seeds, orphans, inherited metadata and repeated
mentions remain present. Repeated metadata cannot generate new endpoint
values. `NativeRootMentionSize` derives list/pool cardinality bounds from
canonical analysis-parser reencoding and complete framed-input parsing;
this is not a claim about the native proof-byte deserializer.
`ClosedByteMachineRootBudget` derives actual input-byte cost from the existing
instruction prices and bounds actual hash keys by executed work. On any actual
closed-interpreter prefix with spent work `W`, the combined charge at a hash
request is at most `(3*W + 256*W^2) / 2^512`. No caller-supplied checkpoint,
source-pool, parser-size or hash-budget certificate is required.

Validation: `scripts/check` passed all 10,601 build jobs and its strict

This per-hash envelope now feeds the first-failure and lifetime work bounds
above. The proof uses an analysis-only work split, rather than assuming a
finite second moment.
Application coverage on the closed instruction clock, honest/verifier actor
cost separation, original registry ownership, independent public extraction,

claimed.

Early receipt events now have a first-moment work bound on the same closed
interpreter prefixes. `ClosedByteMachineLogWork` derives that actual observed
receipt-prefix guesses are bounded by spent instruction work. This uses the
already defined prices; it does not define work as log length. Hash keys and
partial positive receipt reads contribute candidates; starts and empty reads
do not. Duplicate guesses are retained in the log and deduplicated only in
the target set used by the probability bound.

`ClosedByteMachineReceiptWork` splits the analysis at an arbitrary positive
work threshold `T`. Low-work prefix charges are bounded by
`(T / 2^576 + 2^-512) * expectedWork`; Markov pays the whole large-work branch
by `expectedWork / T`. The native execution has no threshold or lifetime cap,
and both incomplete and infinite work tails remain included. The numerical
choice `T = 2^256` certifies a total receipt coefficient at most `2^-255`.
The combined field/column/receipt lifetime event has coefficient
`17/2^141 + 2^-255`, under the earlier Goldilocks role/constructor premises.
This is an event/work theorem in the declared interpreter units, without a
finite-mean premise, completion normalization or success floor.

Validation: `scripts/check` passed all 10,593 build jobs and its strict

Fourteen new guards confirm only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
Regression tests include partial and duplicate receipt guesses, hash-key

Root/source hazards now have the lifetime interpreter-work coupling above;
the earlier explicit global charge supremum remains available. Application false-acceptance coverage must be connected to the
closed instruction clock. Actor separation, honest verification and submission
costs, randomized initialization, physical pricing, public extraction,
registry/context binding, BabyBear execution and strict backend refinement
remain required. No complete 128-bit application theorem is claimed.

A closed byte instruction interpreter now supplies explicit local execution
steps. Its finite instruction syntax contains no evaluator or oracle
continuation supplied by an adversary. Register/stack operations, branches,
public-data copying, starts, hashes and reads execute through this interpreter.
Reads may obtain their offset and length from earlier response bytes. Halt,
reject, empty-pop failure and out-of-code abort pay for the executed instruction
and then stutter without further work. Initialization charges finite owned code,
private tapes and zeroed registers; immutable public setup is excluded and is
charged when copied. This is a specified byte-work schedule, still requiring a
physical implementation/refinement argument.

`ClosedByteMachine` proves exact per-instruction accounting and its finite
sum, prefix resumption, monotone work, terminal stuttering and replay.
`ClosedByteMachineHistory` locates first exposure by the actual instruction
clock and recovers the exact earlier full mixed history. Silent steps insert no
fake observations. `ClosedByteMachineRequest` proves its generated next-request
classifier agrees with each actual interpreter operation and derives the
existing first-read selector at that instruction boundary. The classifier's
`done next` for a local instruction is a single-instruction view, not termination
of the interpreter.

`ClosedByteMachineWork` proves measurability and equality between expected
lifetime work and the supremum of prefix means, retaining incomplete and
infinite tails. `ClosedByteMachineRootLifetime` transports the global
root/source hazard bound to these instruction prefixes with the full causal
prelude and shared caches. Its hazard charges are still explicit.
`ClosedByteMachineGoldRisk` proves that compatible Goldilocks roles with
`Q ≥ 544` have lifetime field/column exposure-event probability at most
`(17 / 2^141) * expectedWork` for this closed interpreter. The proof sums actual
instruction costs, makes stopped exposure charges zero, and uses the earlier
native conditional field/column laws at the exact replayable packet. It has no
runtime cap, observation-count cost proxy, completion conditioning or success
floor.

Validation: `scripts/check` passed all 10,591 build jobs and its strict

an empty oracle log, byte wraparound, halt/reject/abort, public-copy cost,
response-dependent offsets/counts, shared SHAKE/hash coordinates, empty reads
and an exposure whose instruction index differs from its observation index.

This earlier event is the field/column exposure component. The receipt
component is now bounded above; root/source hazards still need work coupling.
Actual application false acceptance must be reduced to the closed-prefix
events. Honest verifier
work, submission costs and actor separation need explicit implementation and

Randomized adversary initialization, native physical-cost simulation, efficient
public extraction, first-original registry binding, BabyBear execution and

is claimed.

Candidate native-role calibration is now kernel checked. For every role quota
`Q ≥ 544`, the rectangular error is at most `17 / 2^141`; the sum over
four roles is at most `17 / 2^139`. Multiplying that sum by the 64-shape
arithmetic allowance and `2^128` gives at most `17/32`. This is an arithmetic
certificate, not an application soundness or physical-work theorem. The
64 shapes are a structural domain, not a bound on attacker trials. Native
query defaults are unchanged.

Validation: `scripts/check` passed all 10,583 build jobs and its strict

`RectangularPCSParameters` uses proximity `(δ/p)^w` and the maximum of the
two shared ordered-column miss terms. Its finite and extended-real versions
agree exactly. `NativeGoldBatchArithmetic` identifies those terms with the
actual native analysis losses, under successful code construction and the
primitive-root premise. `NativeGoldBatchCalibration` bounds both losses and
per-packet risks and discharges the lifetime theorem's width/radius premises
for compatible Goldilocks roles. The resulting lifetime bound retains all
hash, receipt and exposure charges, including the arbitrary causal prelude.
It does not turn exposure count into physical work. BabyBear currently has
these numerical certificates, not the corresponding native execution bridge.

Next obligations are the closed physical instruction machine and cost coupling
(including initialization, local work, aborts/rejections and role separation),
whole-protocol error accounting, first-original registry/context binding,
independent public evaluation/extraction, and strict Rust/backend refinement
including decoding, NTT, SIMD, Div64 and scheduling. Trusted profile dimensions
must also be connected to actual application construction.

The combined lifetime theorem now uses a column selector restricted to the
fixed native ordered quota and complete field coefficient count. Native
preparation derives both equalities at the actual first column read, and the
accepted-run causal coverage proof transports that event through the filter.
No eligibility certificate is added to the verifier or failure witness. Each
active column charge is exactly the fixed-quota loss, equivalently the maximum
of the two shared miss terms at distances `Code.minDist - radius` and
`radius + 1`. The filtered charge is pointwise and lifetime-wise no larger
than the earlier broad charge. Context transport and arbitrary-batch lifetime
composition preserve these tighter events and charges.

Regression tests distinguish quota three from two distinct transport jobs.
A valid foreign one-draw nonce receives the broad charge `31/32` but zero
filtered charge; the native request retains `(31/32)^3`. A nonce with an
incompatible coefficient count is also excluded. Foreign prequeries remain
in the global history and can freeze the same earlier source log. The filter
changes neither native verification nor shared oracle/cache semantics.
Fourteen new theorem guards audit the sampler, native preservation and
context-transport proofs. Whole-protocol calibration, physical cost coupling,
public application extraction, registry/context binding at that boundary,
BabyBear and strict implementation refinement remain open.

Validation for trusted-quota column charging: `scripts/check` passed all

A combined lifetime probability bound now covers false claims across all
accepted native batches with the fixed public parameters and transcript profile. The batch root,
parent input, opening, scheduler, private memory and native verification budget
may vary; no union factor over those batches or response groups is added.
Changing the verifier context while keeping its public parameters fixed
leaves the causal events unchanged. The bound combines one global source/hash hazard supremum
with the early-receipt, first-field proximity and shared-column lifetime
charges. The any-batch failure event is measurable: complete-history replay
preserves accepted work and the canonical field view used by the analysis
extractor, without countability assumptions on scheduler or memory types.

Finite causal oracle preludes are rebased into the same machine before the
unbounded continuation. An exact log bridge preserves every prelude read and
hash and resets no history or cache. The resulting `prelude_bound` charges
exposures during the prelude and leaves no uncharged inherited-exposure
probability. For an arbitrary replayable past without a causal-program origin,
the more general bound retains its inherited term explicitly. This reification
is chronological; it does not assert a physical cost for local callbacks.

The combined bound is still against the recovered-source analysis extractor,
under constructor, primitive-root, native framing/allocation and radius
obligations. It is not yet public PBS application soundness or the 128-bit
expected-work theorem. The native quota and coefficient-count filter above
now removes foreign smaller-quota charges while preserving accepted coverage;
numerical calibration and physical cost coupling remain open.
Trusted registry/context binding at the application boundary, independent
public extraction, physical initialization/local/abort/reject accounting,
BabyBear and backend implementation refinement remain open. Regression tests
cover context variation, retained partial prelude exposure, actual native
verification rebased from a prelude, arbitrary-memory measurability and the
combined lifetime bound. Sixteen new theorem guards audit dependencies.

Validation for lifetime composition: `scripts/check` passed all 10,571 build

axioms; the prelude log bridge and failure rebasing use only `propext`, and

tests and guards are imported through the main test root.

Accepted native false claims in a complete causal machine prefix now derive
their own first-column packet and, for proximity, their earlier first-field
packet and exact history split. Native execution supplies both positive
stream-touch facts. The generic stream-lineage theorem retains starts, empty
reads and hashes before the first positive read and works at arbitrary byte
offsets. The native coverage theorem assumes a replayable prelude and derives
truthful full history from it. Its explicit outcomes are an inherited column
or field exposure, global source disagreement, early receipt at an earlier
machine prefix, field proximity at an earlier prefix, or the concrete column
event at an earlier prefix. No first-read, source-log consistency, receipt
knowledge or truthful-history certificate is supplied by the caller.

Falsity here is still original-query disagreement against the full history's
recovered-source analysis extractor. This does not yet provide public PBS
semantics or independent public extraction. The combined lifetime theorem
above charges finite causal preludes and
combines the event branches with the global source/hash hazard; arbitrary
replayable pasts retain an explicit inherited term. Trusted registry/context
selection at the application boundary remains open.
Physical expected-work coupling, 128-bit calibration, BabyBear instantiation
and implementation refinement remain open. Regression tests exercise mixed
stream lineage, partial inherited exposure, an actual native verifier entirely
after a clean causal prelude, and native verification inherited at machine
fuel zero.

Validation for causal accepted-run coverage: `scripts/check` passed all

The native first-field proximity event now has a causal conditional bound
and an unbounded lifetime charge. The source word is selected from the
history before that field stream's first positive read. An exact equivalence
maps the ordered native coefficients to the rectangular matrix in lane-major
order. It preserves the actual completed collector; no completion mass is
conditioned away. The charge is `(Code.minDist / card Goldilocks)^testWidth`,
with independent test and code-symbol widths, and is zero for an incompatible
parsed coefficient count or a source that is not far. All native candidate
budgets share one loss. The later concrete proximity obstruction enters this
event using a recorded first-read split and the same recovered source log,
even with subsequent hashes in the column history.

The direct transport lemma takes the earlier first-field packet and its
history split; the causal accepted-run theorem above derives both. Finite causal prelude exposures are now charged by rebasing. Binding
trusted context/registry profiles at the application boundary, independent
public extraction, expected physical work and implementation refinement

three-test/six-source-row layout with code-symbol width four, quotient-power

charging. Nine theorem guards audit the new proof dependencies.

Validation for the first-field proximity step: `scripts/check` passed all

At the actual first positive column read, an accepted false native claim
against the recovered-source analysis extractor now has explicit pointwise

If an old field read exists, the first-field source recovered from that

is hidden in the top cover theorem. All original finishing claims remain
available to the false-claim witness reduction.

This is coverage at an actual first-column packet, not yet a full accepted-PBS
application theorem. It still requires original-query falsity against the
analysis extractor, an actual native first-read witness, truthful history,

The causal wrapper derives the first-field and first-column witnesses.
Trusted registry/profile selection, independent public extraction, physical

histories and actual accepted native runs; six new theorem guards check the
allowed axiom set.

Validation for this coverage step: `scripts/check` passed all 10,559 build

The unchanged combined HasteBoots smoke module was validated through the

The parsed column nonce now reproduces the native ordered draw vector,
including duplicates, directly from equality of complete request inputs. No
prior receipt knowledge is required. Actual native acceptance transports all

bridge retains the existing global no-disagreement assumption. Regression
coverage includes three draws `[7,1,7]` producing two deduplicated jobs and an
accepted execution whose first field read precedes a later hash. Full application
false-claim coverage, causal exposure lineage, trusted-profile exposure
