## Raw native field representatives and wire encodings

Inspection of `sumcheck::batch::verify` confirmed that its ordered messages
and initial claims are serialized field objects. Canonical mathematical
field values cannot simply be serialized in their place: Goldilocks keeps
lazy u64 representatives, while BabyBear stores canonical Montgomery u32
representatives. This was a prerequisite for a faithful native scalar-batch
compiler; that verifier has not yet been compiled.

`NativeFieldRepresentation` defines the raw domains and their mathematical
values. For Goldilocks, one conditional subtraction is proved sufficient
for every u64, with exact agreement with the mathematical field value and
native canonical-comparison semantics. The raw word itself is retained.
For BabyBear, the natural-word model explicitly represents low-word masking,
wrapping u64 subtraction, high-word extraction and wrapping u32 correction
of `from_monty`. Its canonical output, radix congruence and mathematical
field value are proved. The conversion to/from the canonical Montgomery
word is a bijection. Relevant `new` and Montgomery-multiplier products are
proved to fit a u64. This is a proof of the stated natural-number word
semantics; checked Rust/instruction refinement and other field arithmetic
operations remain open.

`NativeIntegerPrefix` supplies a self-delimiting integer reader and counted
vector reader, with suffix-preserving left-inverse theorems on the standard
encoder and an injective vector encoding. These are structural helper
readers, not a strict canonical decoder for adversarial proof bytes. In
particular the helper reader may accept a wider spelling of a small value;
no full native deserializer-equivalence claim is made.

`NativeFieldWire` serializes raw base words and degree-prefixed binomial
extension sequences, with injectivity on those raw objects and exact basis
coordinate interpretation. BabyBear mathematical extension values determine
a unique raw representation; this is deliberately not asserted for lazy
Goldilocks. Base-field column-slice encodings and their exact native
`HasteBoots/mw-column/v1` hash-input prefix are also modeled and proved
injective. This does not assume those inputs are disjoint from other hash
roles, nor instantiate the complete Merkle commitment/extraction schedule.

A native Rust fixture confirmed that raw Goldilocks zero and raw modulus
compare equal but have different wire bytes, including inside a degree-three
extension. It also confirmed BabyBear's Montgomery-one spelling, degree-six
extension prefix, raw representative conversions and rejection at the prime,
and both base-field column payload formats. Thus no canonical-value encoder
has been substituted for the native raw message bytes.

Raw results of native Goldilocks arithmetic still need refinement before
computing the scalar batch's initial claim bytes. The optimized interpolation
and independent common-challenge batch, remaining lookup/PBS bodies,

`NativeGoldArithmetic` now retains the literal natural-word carry/borrow
steps of `modulus/goldilocks/ops.rs` for addition and subtraction. It proves

exactly the input's field value. These are proofs of explicit natural-word
semantics, not a checked extraction or assembly-instruction equivalence.

native coordinate-comparison predicate is equivalent to mathematical
extension equality; therefore the individual sumcheck recurrence is checked
without changing the raw storage or its serialized bytes. Its `tableSum`
retains the native ordered zip/fold, including shorter-input truncation,
and proves its mathematical sum of multiplicity-scaled inverse values.
The supplied inverse words have not yet been computed by a refined native
extension inversion algorithm.

## Raw degree-three multiplication and inversion

`NativeGoldInverse` models the Goldilocks addition chain in
`modulus/goldilocks::try_inverse`, including its initial canonicalization
and the canonicalization inside every specialized `exp_acc` power-of-two
call. Repeated squaring has a general field-power theorem. The chain is
proved to compute exponent `p-2`, and Fermat's theorem identifies its value
with inversion on nonzero inputs. The explicit option-valued base inverse
fails exactly at semantic zero, including raw zero and raw modulus. This
is the stated natural-word model of the specialized operations; a checked
Rust/control-flow refinement of `pow_reduce` and the inversion chain remains
required. The remaining generic exponent paths have not yet been refined.

`NativeGoldCubic` retains every operation in the native Karatsuba product,
with constant seven, and proves its three coordinate formulas. The checked
basis is expanded as a polynomial in the adjoined root, whose cube is seven.
These results prove that the raw product denotes mathematical multiplication
in the degree-three lookup field, while preserving the actual lazy words.

`NativeGoldCubicInverse` retains the native determinant, adjugate and final
left scalar multiplication. Their coordinate identities prove that input
times adjugate equals the embedded determinant. Irreducibility of `X^3-7`
rules out a zero adjugate on a nonzero input, and hence the scalar determinant
is nonzero. The literal base addition chain therefore succeeds and the
result denotes the inverse extension value. Division first performs this
inverse and then the native right multiplication; its successful result is
proved to denote field division. `none` represents a failed arithmetic
precondition: unchecked Rust inversion panics there. It is not claimed to
be a graceful native verifier rejection. The accepted nonzero-domain theorem
avoids that path.

A fixture using the pinned Rust algebra crate supplies raw base inverse
outputs for eight boundary words, including both zero representatives, and
raw Karatsuba and inverse outputs for seven degree-three vectors with
canonical and lazy coordinates. The native fixture checks each nonzero
inverse by multiplication. Kernel regressions reproduce all captured words
and the explicit failed arithmetic precondition. They do not normalize
results before comparison, so equality of field values alone cannot make
these regressions pass.

These modules complete the explicit natural-word Goldilocks cubic arithmetic
needed by the lookup compression and reciprocal producers. Linking those
producers to the existing sampler, helper and table-sum compiler is next;
the independent common-challenge scalar batch and optimized interpolation
still require refinement. BabyBear arithmetic, full protocol/PBS/commitment
composition, checked Rust/scheduler correspondence, unbounded chronological
attacker-work coupling, strict proof-byte decoding, numerical losses and the
final application 128-bit security theorem remain open.

The native Goldilocks reciprocal policy evaluates `EF::one() / denominator`.
Its producer must retain the final Karatsuba multiplication by one in
`divResult`; byte equality with the raw `inverseResult` alone has not been
established. This distinction matters when linking the new arithmetic to
serialized helper/claim values.

offset fails the actual fixed-table acceptance predicate, and the middle

request markers, zero-repetition requests, active jobs, completion and the

## Raw helper construction and the packed PCS source

`NativeGoldHelper.fill` copies the selected raw extension words, stops at
capacity, and pads remaining cells with raw extension zero. Accessed invalid
indices are explicit failed preconditions; unread trailing indices are
ignored. Its exact copy/truncate/pad theorem and length theorem hold on the
actual result. Mapping the output words to the degree-three field is proved
to equal the existing `NativeLookupHelper.fill`, including failure paths.

The raw coefficient packer copies all three stored Goldilocks coordinates
in declared basis order and appends raw zero lanes. Every row-major address
is proved to return its exact raw word. Packing with width at least three is
injective on raw extension objects; equal field values cannot be substituted
for equal storage. Its field projection is exactly the old basis coefficient
packer for all widths, with the checked constructor enforcing adequate width.

`NativeGoldHelperPrepared` retains the existing 64-bit helper geometry checks,
explicit geometry/index errors, and the actual raw flat storage. Successful
preparation has exactly `2^numVars * width` words below the 64-bit size limit,
and its projected table satisfies the existing packed-table validity
predicate. Both raw building and preparation project to the old semantic
constructors. The initialized-execution composition theorem supplies the
actual raw reciprocal vector from the sampler's retained first/last draws;
no caller-provided inverse-value certificate is needed for this comparison.

The PCS query theorem evaluates the actual successfully filled raw helper
through its projected row-major source and returns the same encoded extension
MLE as the existing query proof. An accepted wrong extension claim therefore
forces a wrong base-field PCS claim, including the zero-variable post-map
case. This constructor specifies honest helper generation. It does not
restrict adversarial committed padding to zero; the existing PCS interface
for arbitrary unused lanes and adversarial source interpretation remains
necessary for application soundness.

The Rust fixture directly calls the pinned public
`snarks::packed_extension::table` constructor after evaluating the literal
native copy loop. It confirms meaningful lazy coordinates are retained and
padding lanes are raw zero. It also checks native geometry errors and an
unread invalid trailing index. The resolved `concrete-ntt` commit matches
the pinned native lockfile. Kernel regressions reproduce its raw filled and
packed vectors, and cover an accessed invalid index, geometry-first failure,
constant helpers, the variable-count/multiplication overflow boundaries,

Preparation is a checked natural-word model. Its explicit preflight errors
do not claim Rust panic/error-order correspondence. These are pre-row-code

## Scalar-batch statement and round-message wire encodings

`NativePrefixCodec` composes raw usize words, products, bounded vectors and
fixed-degree sequences using suffix-preserving prefix left inverses. Each
constructed encoding has a unique decoded value and following suffix; in
particular its encoder is injective. The codec structures carry their
encoding-law proofs, and the concrete combinators are audited along with
the public theorems. Vector counts retain the native 64-bit usize bound.

`NativeScalarBatchWire` gives the exact Goldilocks payloads used by
`sumcheck::batch::{bind,challenge}`. `PolynomialInfo` writes maximum
multiplicands before number of variables. The statement tuple contains a
separately counted info slice and claim slice. Each extension value retains
its degree-three sequence prefix and three raw u64 coordinates. A round
packet contains the raw usize round index and counted ordered prover
messages; each single-field `ProverMsg` contributes its counted evaluation
vector. Borrowed message references introduce no additional wire wrapper.
Lazy Goldilocks coordinates are retained throughout.

The statement and round encoders are injective and their structural readers
preserve arbitrary following bytes on constructed messages. Binding either
payload to the existing native framed transcript is also injective at fixed
prior transcript input, under the explicit native frame-byte length bound.
A vector-count bound alone is not claimed to bound total encoded payload
bytes. These input-binding theorems do not assert collision freedom of
oracle outputs or global disjointness from other oracle-input roles.

The isolated Rust fixture directly serializes the pinned public
`PolynomialInfo` and `ProverMsg` types in the same borrowed tuple/slice forms
used by the private batch functions. It confirms the complete statement and
round payloads, wide usize metadata, separate counts, empty evaluation
messages and empty packet layouts. Kernel regressions reproduce every
captured byte. Suffix-preserving structured round trips use the proved
left-inverse laws and those independently checked byte encodings; deciding
equality of the dependent record objects directly hits Lean reduction limits.

These are payload encoders and structural readers. They do not implement or
validate the batch's native proof-shape/degree preflight, independent
recurrences, common challenge, optimized interpolation or terminal checking.
The encoding fixtures deliberately include empty messages which native
preflight would reject. The readers may accept a wider integer spelling of
zero, as the regression records; they are not a strict-canonical proof-byte
decoder or a Rust decoder resource/error-order refinement. No artificial
runtime iteration cap or claimed machine-work charge is introduced.

## Scalar-batch preflight and checked round extraction

`NativeScalarBatchPreflight` now models the verifier's ordered front end.

dimensions, and interpolation-node collisions, before binding any statement
bytes. The error categories remain separate. The native usize `degree + 1`
overflow check is retained before evaluation-vector length checks. Successful
shape is characterized by a `Forall₂` relation between every trusted info
and its proof instance, including all round counts and evaluation counts.

The actual consecutive-node loop uses raw extension addition by one and
canonical field-zero comparison after every addition. Its theorem covers
all intermediate nodes. Starting from raw zero it accepts exactly degrees
below the Goldilocks characteristic. The characteristic follows from the
injective base-field algebra map into the checked degree-three extension.
Positive-degree and common-variable-count conditions follow from successful
preflight; no interpolation domain or degree certificate is supplied by the
caller. There is no introduced runtime iteration cap or replacement fast
range check. The characteristic boundary regression uses this universal
loop theorem rather than evaluating a characteristic-sized loop.

Each recurrence reads the first two actual message evaluations and compares
their raw sum using native semantic equality. The checker is the ordered
zip of these independent checks. Under the validated length invariant it is
exactly a `Forall₂` assertion checking every claim, and compensating errors
in two claims are rejected. Its round-binding helper rejects before any
round-message absorption. These are phase helpers, not a complete verifier:
standalone zip checks still have native truncation semantics, and the full
round driver must retain the proved count invariant after interpolation.

message with an explicit failed-access result and no default message.
Accepted preflight and an in-range round prove extraction succeeds in
statement order, its packet count fits usize and equals the claim count,

proves the first-two-entry access is safe for every matched equation.

## Literal scalar interpolation and raw field interpretation

`NativeInterpolationCore` now models the pinned private
`sumcheck/src/verifier.rs::interpolate_uni_poly` operation order: the
consecutive-node scan and early return, difference/product accumulation,
factorial loop, and descending interpolation accumulator. The numerator is
left-associated exactly as in Rust. The last interpolation step does not
perform the nonfinal denominator/counter updates. The factorial retains its
last counter update. The model has no replacement Lagrange evaluator,
normalization, default array entry or runtime cap. Empty input, missing
entries and failed inversion are explicit `none`; the corresponding native
unchecked precondition fails by panic rather than graceful rejection.

The core's homomorphism theorem preserves the complete partial result for
any arithmetic interpretation preserving every primitive, including
Boolean equality and partial division. Intermediate scan, factorial and
reverse-state maps are proved separately. A successful scan's node index
lies in the tested interval; an off-node scan retains exactly one difference
per input evaluation. Zero-node return preserves the original stored word.

`NativeInterpolationField` supplies ordinary field operations with checked
zero division and proves both factorial state components equal the natural
factorial and the next counter. `NativeGoldInterpolation` instantiates the
core with the proved raw lazy Goldilocks operations, exact Karatsuba cubic
multiplication and native cubic inversion/division. It proves raw equality
matches field equality and that all semantic-zero cubic representatives
fail inversion. Together with the nonzero inversion theorem, this gives a
total, branch- and failure-preserving division interpretation. The resulting
`interpolate_value` theorem maps the entire raw computation to the same
literal field loop, with no success certificate or nonzero-denominator
premise supplied by the caller. This is representation refinement; the
field loop's Lagrange/polynomial correspondence and nonfailure under valid

## Interpolation safety follows from actual preflight

`NativeInterpolationSafety` now proves a precise field description of the
literal scan. Its retained list is exactly the consecutive differences
`point - j`, including the zero node, its product is their product and its
check counter is the final node. A successful off-node scan rules out
zero in every retained difference. The preflight's condition that every
positive cast through the degree is nonzero implies a nonzero factorial.

The descending loop's safety proof maintains its actual remaining-node
counter and nonzero `up` accumulator. The count relation ensures that every
nonfinal multiplication by the negated counter is nonzero. It proves every
list access and division succeeds; no product/nonzero assertion or success
certificate is supplied by the interpolation caller. Combined with the
scan index bounds, this proves the whole literal field interpolation is
total for every challenge whenever its input is nonempty and its node
range passes the native check. The proof covers singleton diagnostic
inputs as well as all positive degrees accepted by the batch verifier.
There is no runtime cap or restriction to lookup degrees 1, 3 and 4.

The same checked node condition makes consecutive casts injective. At
every node the actual scan takes the matching early return, and field
interpolation returns exactly that received entry. These are proofs about
the literal implementation, rather than only the mathematical interpolant.

`NativeGoldInterpolationSafety` transports totality back through the full
raw-to-field interpretation. Its raw known-node theorem transports the
scan branch itself, so it proves exact original-word return, including
lazy challenge and evaluation representatives; semantic equality of the
result alone would not justify that claim. No canonicalization is inserted.

The bridge obtains nonzero casts from `nodesFrom_iff`, not an independent
characteristic or denominator certificate. Successful actual dimensions
and a matched message width therefore imply raw interpolation succeeds.
The ordered-round theorem combines actual proof shape, dimensions and
in-range extraction: the resulting packet has exactly the claim count and
every equation interpolates successfully at any common challenge. The
regression consumer derives those preconditions directly from a successful
`beginVerify` result. These theorems do not assume a completed round driver.

Regression consumers cover arbitrary raw messages and challenges through
the full characteristic-sized node range without evaluating or imposing a
cap on a characteristic-sized validation loop, exact arbitrary raw node
returns, and the actual preflight/round packet connection. A kernel test
also retains failed standalone inversion for a malformed reverse step;
valid preflight execution is proved to avoid that failure.

The off-node loop's Lagrange/polynomial correspondence remains open.
Safety and representation refinement do not establish it. Subsequent
work must prove that correspondence, implement and connect the actual
common-challenge round driver and terminal authentication, then complete
scalar-batch soundness. Full lookup/PBS extraction, checked Rust/scheduler
and strict decoder refinement, BabyBear arithmetic, chronological
attacker-work coupling, numerical certification and the final 128-bit
application security theorem also remain open.

## Literal scalar interpolation has polynomial semantics

The previously open off-node interpolation correspondence is now proved.
`NativeInterpolationWeights` identifies the signed factorial denominator
with the product of consecutive-node differences omitting its own node,
and hence with Mathlib's Lagrange nodal weight. The adjacent-index identity
matches both native updates, `up *= -remaining` and `down *= index`,
without replacing either update by an inverse operation. These identities
cover every degree admitted by the node check, with no restriction to the
current lookup degrees.

`NativeInterpolationAccumulator` keeps both actual denominator accumulators
in the execution. Its invariant is `up = down * denominator(index)` with
nonzero `down`. The exact nonfinal counter updates preserve that invariant.
Each checked division is proved equal to its barycentric summand only in
the mathematical interpretation; the literal raw operation order remains
unchanged. Induction over the actual descending loop proves the final
result is the initial accumulator plus the complete finite partial sum.
The final-index early stop is included, and there are no default entries,
iteration caps or caller-supplied evaluation correctness certificates.

`NativeInterpolationPolynomial` constructs a polynomial directly from the
received evaluation list and its validated width. Its natural degree is
at most the trusted degree, and it takes the received values at every
node. The actual scan's retained product equals the nodal polynomial's
evaluation. The descending-loop sum therefore equals the barycentric
Lagrange evaluation at every off-node point. Combining that theorem with
the scan's known-node branch proves the whole literal field interpolation
returns the constructed polynomial's evaluation for every challenge.

`NativeGoldInterpolationPolynomial` transports the result through the
full raw Goldilocks representation theorem. The complete partial raw
computation maps to `some` of the received polynomial's evaluation. No
successful execution, independently bounded polynomial or nonzero
denominator certificate is a premise. The node condition comes from the
literal native `nodesFrom` check. The first-two-entry raw recurrence is
proved equivalent to `P(0) + P(1) = claim` in the extension field. Successful
actual dimensions supply all positivity and node conditions for every
matched equation, giving both its derived degree bound and its actual raw
interpolation semantics.

Kernel regressions recompute two native Rust off-node golden vectors
(linear and cubic, including lazy coordinates and a near-u64-maximum
input), and then use the new theorem to identify those outputs with the
received polynomial's evaluation. Universal regression consumers cover
arbitrary messages and challenges throughout the full characteristic
range, and combine actual successful metadata, derived degree bounds,
raw interpolation and the native polynomial recurrence.

This closes the scalar interpolation arithmetic/polynomial correspondence,
not the entire scalar verifier or its soundness proof. The actual
common-challenge round driver, ordered updated claims and terminal
authentication still need implementation and composition. Full lookup/PBS
extraction, remaining helper/PCS bodies and child/parent linking, checked
Rust/scheduler and strict decoder refinement, BabyBear arithmetic,
chronological attacker-work coupling, numerical certification and the
final 128-bit application security theorem remain open.

## Actual common-challenge scalar verifier loop

`NativeScalarBatchUpdate` now implements the native expected-vector mutation
through a zip with the actual round messages. A missing message leaves the
remaining expected entries untouched; extra messages are ignored. These
malformed-state semantics are retained rather than replacing the loop by
a potentially truncating map of messages. Successful updates preserve the
original expected length. Under the validated count equality, a `Forall₂`
theorem proves each message updates exactly its corresponding output in
statement order. Interpolation success follows from the existing actual
preflight/message safety theorem.

`NativeScalarBatchVerifier` compiles the complete raw independent-scalar
round driver into the existing online oracle program. It runs actual
preflight, collects the actual ordered round messages, checks every
recurrence before any round binding, binds the native round packet,
starts the typed scalar request with the Goldilocks degree-three descriptor
and native challenge label, collects actual canonical coefficients, decodes
their raw word and performs literal interpolation updates. Only then does
it append the one shared challenge to the point and advance the round.
Finished output maps every ordered expected value to a subclaim carrying
a clone of that same point. These are unauthenticated subclaims, exactly
as in native `batch::verify`; caller-side terminal authentication is not
silently supplied by this model.

The machine retains active coefficient readers, rejected chunks, receipt
state and completed-round records. A completed-round record stores the
actual packet, canonical challenge coefficients, raw challenge and prior
and updated expected vectors; it adds no native transcript frames. One
analysis tick drives one candidate while sampling. Prefix exhaustion
returns the active machine instead of a native rejection, and the exact
execution-addition theorem resumes without repeating completed requests
or receipts. Program execution is proved equal to the direct interpreter,
and every compiled prefix has the existing counterfactual replay property.
Native rejection and finished states stutter without further queries.

`NativeScalarBatchVerifierInvariant` proves the expected count, trusted
round bound, ordered completed challenge list, and common point throughout
arbitrary analysis prefixes. Active requests retain the actual packet
widths/count, passed individual recurrence checks and canonical sampler
validity. From successful real preflight, all internal checked-model
failures are unreachable: any failed execution is specifically a native
individual-recurrence rejection. Finished runs return exactly the original
claim count, every subclaim has the same point, and that point has the
trusted number of variables. The explicit internal access/decode/inversion
failures are checked precondition failures, not additional reachable native
rejection paths.

Kernel regressions cover two equations across two actual rounds, updated
claims and their common point, exact observation counts, rejection of a
second-round recurrence before binding or challenge, an all-rejecting oracle
retained as a pending request at prefix exhaustion, and rejection followed
by successful canonical collection retaining the full consumed-byte sequence.
Malformed standalone zip cases retain the native untouched-tail/ignored-
extra behavior. A universal regression consumes successful `beginVerify`
and the no-internal-failure theorem without extra safety certificates.

A separate isolated fixture calls pinned public `sumcheck::batch::verify`
for two rounds and independent equations. Its reference transcript uses
the actual shared challenges and verbatim included private interpolation
body from the pinned verifier source. It compares exact raw subclaims,
common-point coordinates and transcript continuation. A corrupted second
recurrence rejects against the actual first-round interpolated claim and
retains exactly the transcript after round zero. This is native regression
evidence, not a checked Rust-to-Lean refinement or machine-work theorem.

Per-round polynomial meaning must still be connected to the retained
completed-round history and the soundness/extraction argument. Terminal
claims need authentication in the actual lookup/PCS caller. Full lookup/PBS
bodies and child/parent linking, checked Rust/scheduler and strict decoder
refinement, BabyBear arithmetic, chronological attacker-work coupling,
numerical certification and the final 128-bit application theorem remain
open. The driver and structural invariants do not establish those claims.

## Actual scalar history supplies the polynomial terminal contract

`NativeScalarBatchHistory` now derives a chained history from actual
initialized verifier execution. The chain begins with the statement's real
ordered claims. Each new link's prior expected vector is the preceding
link's output, its round ordinal is the prior history length, and its
packet is obtained from the actual submitted proof at that round. Every
completed record retains the passed independent recurrence checks, the
literal successful interpolation update, and the completed canonical scalar
request with its actual decoded raw challenge. Initialization, every tick
and every finite resumed prefix preserve this property. No caller supplies
a chain, trace correspondence or successful-draw certificate.

`NativeScalarBatchRoundMeaning` connects those operational records to the
received-vector polynomials. Every matched equation has the trusted degree
bound, its received polynomial satisfies `P(0) + P(1) = prior`, and the
actual interpolation output is `P(r) = next` at the retained common
challenge. The interface explicitly retains equal original counts for
infos, messages, prior claims and next claims, so its zipped per-equation
relation cannot silently omit a slot. The challenge is proved equal to
assembly of the actual completed coefficient list, with exact canonical
raw coordinates at every basis index.

`NativeScalarBatchContract` combines these results with the completed
verifier's structural invariants. Every successful actual run supplies
consecutive proof rounds of exactly the trusted variable count, a chain
from the original sums to the final ordered values, and exactly the
returned subclaims at the common point formed by those retained draws.
Every original equation remains present. The terminal output's expected
vector is the endpoint of that same chain; its common point has the trusted
length. The proof constructs the received polynomials and execution chain
from the run, rather than assuming independent semantic witnesses.

Kernel regressions observe both actual round packets, their exact prior
and updated raw claims, the consecutive ordinals and coefficient draws in
a two-equation/two-round execution. A finished-control tag from that run
then supplies the complete algebraic contract. Universal consumers cover
all actually completed records of arbitrary initialized prefixes, including
packet-source correspondence, and preserve the chain under a suspended
all-rejecting request. Consecutive ordinals are derived from initialization
without an externally supplied range assertion.

This closes the deterministic operational-to-polynomial history contract
for the scalar verifier. It is not a Fiat--Shamir probability bound or a
terminal authentication proof. The canonical shared lookup caller still
needs its actual helper equality and reciprocal-identity terminal guards,
source/helper query bridge and accepted PCS opening composition. The
existing source-independent terminal adapters are not substituted for those
bodies. Full lookup/PBS extraction and linking, checked Rust/scheduler and
strict decoder refinement, BabyBear arithmetic, chronological attacker-work
coupling, numerical certification and the final 128-bit application theorem
remain open.

## Raw equality, prefix mask and lookup terminal residual

`NativeTerminalBits` now connects the literal unsigned usize shift-and-mask
predicate to the threshold coordinate of the existing low-bit-first address
bijection. The proof handles every coordinate, rather than accepting a
caller-supplied decoded threshold. The native count remains a 64-bit word.

`NativeTerminalCore` retains the exact equality zip/fold, descending point
accesses, `same`/`out` prefix updates and separate full-table shortcut. Each
prefix access is checked, and missing entries are explicit failed internal
preconditions. Its representation theorem preserves the whole partial
result, including failure, through arithmetic homomorphisms. It inserts no
normalization, default point entry or alternative prefix evaluator.

`NativeTerminalField` proves the literal equality fold equals the public
field equality product on equal-dimension points. Its prefix-loop theorem
uses the original coordinates and actual shift bits, then connects the
whole loop to the already proved prefix-mask MLE, including zero count,
empty points and the full-table branch. The unsigned word-shift domain
`point.length < 64` is explicit in this checked model. It is an internal
machine precondition, not a new reachable native rejection or retry cap;
unchecked out-of-domain Rust behavior is not claimed. Deriving that bound
and the logical-prefix bound from the actual caller's public geometry is
still part of the remaining caller/source refinement.

`NativeGoldTerminalArithmetic` instantiates the loops with proved raw lazy
Goldilocks operations and exact cubic multiplication. It also models the
native ordered full-extension compression of decoded source elements and
powers, and the exact association of the masked reciprocal residual. The
complete raw value maps to the same public terminal formula used by
`ExtensionLookupIdentity`. Native canonical-coordinate equality against
the supplied expected value is equivalent to that field identity. Both
zip truncation and raw lazy representatives remain literal.

The interface is deliberately `valueFromElements`/`checkFromElements`:
these elements must still be produced by the actual source query and
padding projection. This arithmetic theorem neither bypasses those checks
nor assumes PCS authentication. The native caller's helper-sum equality,
interleaved claim accesses, source/helper query construction, terminal-value
binding and accepted opening composition remain to implement and connect.

An isolated Rust fixture compiles the verbatim pinned private `equality`,

It calls the real public source-query/projection functions and compares
native acceptance/rejection for exact and one-offset expected values.
Kernel regressions reproduce all twelve small prefix vectors, lazy

cases, the compression output, and four full terminal raw outputs. They
check exact stored words, including outputs above the modulus. Additional
kernel tests exercise explicit bad-shift/missing-access model failures;

uses the field-identity theorem with explicit valid machine geometry.

The remaining lookup caller and PCS/query bridge obligations, full PBS
extraction and linking, checked Rust/scheduler and strict decoder refinement,

certification and the final 128-bit application theorem remain open. The

`NativeGoldProjection` now models the native Goldilocks extension bridge's
actual dimension, usize-square, vector-length and padding checks. Padding

comparison. Lazy zero padding is accepted; meaningful coordinates are
copied without normalization. Success is characterized by all original
raw coordinate getters and the full padding check. Packing followed by

representatives. Its complete partial field interpretation agrees with
`PaddedExtension.element`, including rejected padding.

`NativeGoldMatrix` retains the native row-major payload and checked matrix
shape. Matrix application rejects zero/wrong widths, checked-square
overflow, wrong payload length and wrong vector length. Every row uses the
literal ascending-column raw multiply/add fold from zero. The existing
base addition-fold interpretation is now exposed and reused, so the new
matrix proof does not duplicate the base arithmetic induction. No raw
arithmetic behavior or canonicalization policy changed.

`NativeGoldMatrixMeaning` derives every coefficient from the actual
validated payload. It proves row lengths and every row-major address bound,
then identifies the complete raw application with that matrix's field
product on every original input lane. No separately supplied mathematical
matrix or correctness certificate is used. In particular, original input
padding is not assumed zero when applying a matrix; projection may suppress
an unused lane before the output padding is tested.

`NativeGoldPostMap` models the native optional post-matrix operation and
then the checked extension projection, in that order. An absent post-map
returns the original vector after its native width/length check. A present
post-matrix is validated and applied, with invalid shape still a failure.
The full partial composition agrees with field matrix application followed
by the existing padded-extension decoder. These results cover both success
and failure and do not treat a projection matrix as an ordinary identity.

The pinned Rust fixture calls the real public bridge and matrix functions.
It covers widths 3, 4 and 8; exact lazy coordinate retention; zero-alias

composition and caller geometry also remain to connect. Full lookup/PBS

BabyBear arithmetic, chronological attacker-work coupling, numerical
certification and the final 128-bit application theorem remain open.

## Raw scalar lane maps and ordered checked matrix products

`NativeGoldLaneWeights` models the native low-point enumerated left fold,
retaining its original coordinate order, offset, raw accumulator and
shift-and-mask predicate. Its raw word embedding is proved not to wrap for
any validated lane. The existing matrix-square check derives the machine
lane bound and, for a power-of-two width, the required shift bound; no
arbitrary cap is added. The actual native bits are derived from the same
low-bit address equivalence used by `ExtensionQuery.nativeLanes`, so the
complete raw weight has the established tensor-weight meaning without an
external bit-decoding certificate.

`NativeGoldLaneMatrix` uses the ordered raw column-copy loop to store the
three weight coordinates for every original scalar lane. Only output rows
beyond the extension degree are left zero. Every original source column
participates, including columns ignored by helper extension projection.
The matrix's complete field meaning is derived from its actual payload and
equals the generic lane matrix with those native tensor weights. Applying
and projecting this actual matrix yields the weighted sum of all original
source entries, without an input-padding premise.

`NativeGoldMatrixProductLoop` models the exact native `a,c,b` loop order,
using the raw add/multiply operations. Its invariants show that each inner
loop updates every selected column once, later rows preserve completed
rows, and every final cell retains its ascending-c raw dot-product fold.
A row-major serialization theorem connects each finite-view write to the
corresponding single raw list-set write.

`NativeGoldMatrixProductPayload` then executes those same nested loops on
an actual square-length row-major payload. Every accumulator read carries
its proved address bound, and every list write preserves the full length.
Serialization commutes with each step, each nested loop and the complete
zero-initialized program. Thus the payload correspondence is derived
through execution rather than supplied as a final-matrix certificate.

`NativeGoldMatrixProduct` validates both original matrices against the
left matrix's width, reads each operand by bounded getters into its actual
payload, runs the literal row-major program, and performs the checked final
matrix construction. Malformed operands retain failure. The resulting
field matrix is left times right, in that order. Applying it makes the
right map act first, as required for the native first pair `M(weight) * L`.
These remain raw arithmetic/program models; instruction and scheduler
refinement is still open.

The public Rust fixtures obtain lane matrices from the actual scalar-query
zero-row-variable branch, at widths 4 and 8 and with lazy and Boolean point
coordinates. They cover all raw lane weights, lane payloads, application
and projection. Kernel cases reproduce those raw values and show that
changing the fourth original scalar lane changes the selected result.
The matrix-product fixture covers widths 1, 2 and 4, lazy operands, malformed
left/right payloads, wrong widths and overflow. It also checks that the
actual scalar-query first pair equals forward multiplication by the lane
matrix; reversing the product yields different raw results. The normal-depth
kernel suite checks forward and reversed raw products on those native
payloads, together with universal lane-map and ordered-product consumers.

The outer scalar-query wrapper remains to be connected: the actual
power-of-two and ilog2 checks, checked point-dimension addition, low/high
point split, replacement of the empty helper post-map, and first-pair
mutation must consume these new loop results. Native query folding,
accepted PCS openings, terminal guard composition and caller geometry
remain open. Full lookup/PBS extraction and linking, checked Rust/scheduler
and strict decoder refinement, BabyBear arithmetic, chronological attacker
work, numerical certification and the final 128-bit application theorem
also remain open.

## Backend value policies and gating child initialization

`NativeSharedLookupValues` now models the native used-slot construction and
proof-value validation window. Ordered slot marking retains every request,
including repeated slots, and its flags are true exactly for slots appearing
in the original requests. Earlier numeric preflight supplies index safety;
the checked model's out-of-bounds list updates are not a claim about native
indexing outside that domain. Earlier proof shape supplies complete source
coverage for the native zip loop.

The trusted backend selects the validation policy. Legacy non-hiding
Brakedown `Parameters<C>` retains the trait defaults: base-field value
validation accepts lazy representatives. The response backends for
PolyFRIM require canonical base values. This choice is an argument of the
compiler, not a proof field. Multiplicities and source values follow that
policy; helper extension scalars are always required to have canonical
coordinates. No extra canonical guard is added to the legacy backend.

Unused-source zeros use native field equality, not raw-word equality.
Consequently a lazy Goldilocks zero can pass in an unused legacy source
slot. A nonzero value fails in either policy, and a lazy helper zero fails
in either policy. Successful checking supplies semantic zero for every
unused supplied source coordinate and canonical coordinates for every
helper. With the canonical policy, unused zeros are also literally raw
zero. Original raw values and their wire spelling are retained throughout;
this validator does not normalize proof data.

`NativeSharedLookupValidated` gates the existing operational prelude on
both dimension and value checks. Successful execution supplies both
contracts and the actual original lookup/equality/statement run. Completed
valid runs still construct ready statements under the existing native
vector allocation domain. Rejected checks return no ready output and
issue no prelude observations.

The child-program entry places the actual initializer behind those gates.
Rejection skips its oracle calls entirely. Acceptance executes it once,
retains all of its observations before the prelude, and uses its actual
returned child state. Successful runs derive the full original prelude
contract from this same initializer execution; no parent/child transcript
equality certificate is an input. The stateful child-program entry additionally retains the initializer's
computed parent/private state alongside every ready result for later
finishing and authentication. Its source is identified with the actual
initializer output, without a supplied state-equality certificate. The
exact native multiplicity-bound child initializer and finish binding remain
to instantiate. Earlier PCS context/preflight framing is also separate.

The native fixture compiles the exact used-slot and value-validation
windows extracted from the shared caller, plus the actual legacy default
and unmasked PolyFRIM validation bodies. Native Goldilocks and extension
implementations perform the equality and canonicality checks; minimal
records/error wrappers provide the fields read by those windows. It
checks canonical values, lazy multiplicities, lazy used sources, lazy
unused zeros, nonzero unused sources and noncanonical helper coordinates
under both policies. Kernel regressions reproduce every outcome and test
that rejected gates skip an observable initializer, while accepted gates
preserve its issued observations even if sampling remains suspended.
This is correspondence evidence for the modeled window, not a full native
caller or Rust refinement theorem.

`NativeByteCodec` provides raw u8, byte-vector and fixed-byte-array codecs.

`NativeBrakedownContext` builds the exact Goldilocks Brakedown context input:

and serialization are an explicit trusted interface; their instantiation and

injectivity retain native byte-frame allocation domains and make no
checkpoint-injectivity assumption.

`NativeSharedLookupParent` takes already rebuilt requests and executes the

request's bind message. Registry setup recomputes every source context before
absorbing the complete ordered registry. Alias-group construction and source
claim authentication remain separate; setup framing alone does not establish

Successful context collection preserves source count, so vector bounds used

The new `begin` entry point passes the actual prepared parent into the prior

execution and derives numeric preflight. Rebuilt original configurations

## Computable raw lookup retries and exact projection

`NativeGoldLookupSampler` replaces the operational abstract-field pole
decision with the existing raw-word predicate. It retains the active
coefficient reader, canonical compression/offset words, powers and public
table, every completed draw including rejected offsets, and the offset
rejection count. A rejected coefficient stays in the same reader and at
the same coefficient index. A zero or pole offset is absorbed with its
receipt before another offset request starts. Neither path adds a native
retry cutoff; fuel specifies a resumable analysis prefix only.

Coefficient conversion is total by reduction modulo the field modulus.
It agrees with the abstract scalar interpretation for every input list.
On actual completed canonical coefficient collections it preserves every
original word exactly, with neither defaulting nor reduction. This conversion
applies to fresh challenge coefficients, not to retained Brakedown public
or proof base-field words.

Projection maps the raw selection into `NativeLookupChallenge` and preserves
the exact machine, complete coefficient records, rejected-draw count and
ordered oracle observations after initialization, each tick and any finite
analysis prefix. These are equalities for every world and budget, without a
freshness, probability, completed-draw or row-identification certificate.
The split-budget law retains state/logs across retries. The abstract
`Classical.choice` decision remains a mathematical specification; it is no
longer evaluated on the operational path.

`NativeGoldLookupBatch` preserves literal request ordinals and repetition
order, including request-binding frames. Its projection commutes with the
schedule, initial state, sample completion, each tick and any finite batch
execution. Raw row words map to their field interpretations only in the
abstract projection; runtime selection uses the original raw table.

`NativeSharedLookupPrelude.protocol` now executes the raw batch and compiles
its projection into the existing equality/statement preparation. Its public
`run_protocol` theorem still identifies exactly the same initialized
abstract batch execution and log. Thus all existing prepared-job, statement,
geometry, value-gate, terminal, scalar and child-finish contracts remain in
force through the same caller APIs. No separate ready transcript or
acceptance certificate was added to the full entry point.

The previous test-only accepted-first-offset reconstruction was removed.
All 15 native-fixture regressions now execute
`NativeSharedLookupExecution.protocol` directly for normal completion,
suspension and tampered proofs. They retain exact native reader inputs,
scalar claims, final parent continuation and child-binding checks. The native
fixture's full Rust verifier includes PCS; the Lean result still stops before
PCS authentication. Kernel evaluation of the complete entry point now works
without changing the abstract field's equality instance or using new axioms,
`native_decide`, elevated recursion depth or an attacker-work cutoff.

Sixteen additional kernel examples exercise a scripted ideal world with a
zero offset, a nonzero pole, then a valid offset, retaining all four draws
including the compression draw. They check rejection counts, changed retry
inputs, exact reader counts and a split prefix across both retries. They
also check rejected canonical candidates consume bytes at offsets 0 and 8
without advancing the coefficient index or offset-rejection count, and
check original request/repetition order. The extracted native predicate

## Native PCS wire and concrete column authentication

`NativeGoldPcsWire` supplies exact constructed-wire codecs for a raw matrix
(width followed by its raw Goldilocks word vector), ordered zero/one matrix
pairs, query vectors, `(root, query, values)` binding payloads and
`(ordinal, slot, query, values)` deferred-claim payloads. The helper query
packer calls the actual raw coefficient-query construction and packs only
its PCS pairs. It proves packing succeeds under the existing native matrix
shape and usize count bounds and preserves every matrix. The local extension
post-map is absent from the PCS bytes, including for an empty point. Readers
are structural prefix inverses, not a strict adversarial native decoder.

`NativeHashOracleBridge` compiles hash-only VCVio computations into the same
causal mixed-oracle program used by the transcript, preserving their exact
result and ordered observations for every world. It proves truthful hash logs
replay their original computation from the projected common cache, also when
an arbitrary truthful earlier mixed log is present. Every repeated call is
retained in the log; repeated keys share one cache entry. Neither collision
freedom nor fresh hash inputs are assumed.

`NativeGoldColumnAuthentication` executes the raw whole-column hash and
bottom-up Merkle sibling loop. Its leaf bytes are the native column domain
followed by the original raw word-vector encoding; node bytes are exactly the
two ordered 64-byte digests. Paths include the claimed leaf first. Empty or
wrong-height paths fail without a hash, matching the outer PCS path-shape
gate; the standalone Rust `MerkleTree::check` relies on that gate. Digests use
an explicit byte-list equality decision, so the concrete checker reduces in
the kernel. For a decoded path the program is exactly the compiled existing
`NativeMerkleVerifier.verifyPayload`. Acceptance of a received column derives
a typed path and successful replay of that same payload/path in the common
cache projected from its actual earlier and column observations. No separate
replay or authentication certificate is an input.

## Computed helper-opening handoff from completed lookup execution

`NativeSharedLookupHelpers` extends the actual parent/lookup/equality/scalar/

truncation behavior on malformed vectors.

count. `packet_at` identifies each call with the root, coefficient vector and

## Native base-field and atomic column challenges

`NativePrimeRequest` models the classical typed prime request used by the
Brakedown base-field random linear test. It binds `typed request kind`
(scalar/vector), then `field challenge kind` (`prime vector`), with no
extension descriptor or multiplication table. It reuses the canonical field
collector, preserving every candidate, rejected chunk, suspended reader and
receipt. The count is a native usize; analysis fuel is not a native retry
limit. Completed requests have exactly the original count of canonical
values, and conversion to a raw Goldilocks word preserves each integer
exactly. Split execution/resumption retains the same request and ordered log.

`NativeIndexRequest` models the classical schedule-5 atomic index API. The
nonzero power-of-two domain and checked `count*8` guards precede any transcript
mutation or oracle operation. A valid request appends the raw eight-byte
little-endian domain, then issues one ordinary byte challenge of length
`count*8`. The complete ordered list comes from successive eight-byte words
masked by `domain-1`; it is retained separately from the sorted, deduplicated
transmitted indices. The adapter proves the original quota, every bound,
sortedness, no duplicates and exact original membership. Valid usize domains
also supply the bit bound needed by the finite-byte law. Invalid requests
produce no observations. Count zero still records its start and empty output.

For kernel evaluation, the executable ascending sort uses the library's
structural insertion sort. `distinct_eq_mergeSort` proves equality to the
existing merge-sort/dedup definition on every input, while sortedness and
membership proofs retain the same specification. This identifies the sorted
integer sequence; it is not Rust's `sort_unstable` instruction refinement.
The native whole-block decoder is identified with the typed with-replacement
positions used by the existing column-opening analysis, in literal word order.

`NativeAtomicIndexLaw` splits the whole byte block into discarded high bits
and retained low-bit positions at every word, by a bijection. It proves the
entire vector of positions is jointly uniform for a uniformly fresh block;
no per-word independence premise is supplied. The existing exact column
agreement probability then applies with the original quota, including
repeated positions. These are finite uniform-sample laws. Conditional
freshness in the actual adaptive transcript execution, including earlier
private/verification prequeries, remains a separate composition obligation.

`NativeGoldPcsWire` now also supplies the exact pair-of-vectors response
codec and its kind-1 `mw linear responses` binder. Its original raw words
and both vector headers precede the atomic index request. The native fixture
`/tmp/hasteboots-pcs-challenge-fixture` records a base-field vector, those
responses, atomic draws, sorted indices and the following parent challenge.
It separately records scalar requests, empty prime/index requests, a
one-column domain, and invalid domains/overflow with unchanged continuation.
It invokes the actual native public transcript APIs. This checks the atomic
API, not the trusted caller's feature-flag selection.

## Native single-opening parameter, binding and random-test prefix

`NativeBrakedownParameters` models the checked `Parameters::new_encoded`
constructor for the selected 64-bit machine model. The original code object
supplies message length, block count and block width, together with the same
row description already used by its parameter context. The basic dimension
and query-count guards precede exponentiation; code-message/stride checks
precede checked table, encoded-matrix, linear-test and Merkle-tree sizes.
The returned geometry and native random-test count are computed data.
The constructor proves that the next power-of-two leaf count minimally covers
the code blocks and that every accepted path length is below 64.

No atomic-only domain or quota constraint is added to this constructor. The
native constructor can accept a non-power-of-two code length and very large
nonzero query counts; the atomic index API checks its separate domain and
`count*8` bounds later. Geometry accessors do not certify a code's distance,
encoder correctness, serialization or actual native parameter instantiation.

`NativeGoldPcsOpening` supplies the original non-hiding single-opening record:
raw test/evaluation vectors followed by a vector of raw columns with complete
leaf-first paths. Its codec matches the native struct order and has a proved
constructed-wire prefix inverse. Outer shape gates check both response lengths,
a nonempty column list, the `min(queries, blocks)` cap and every column's value
and path lengths. No column authentication is performed by this shape gate.

`NativeGoldPcsBinding` checks the original query/value counts and every actual
zero/one matrix before computing the code context in the common hash oracle.
Only a successfully serialized context contributes its hash observation.
The original digest, commitment, ordered matrices and raw values are then
appended under the native two binding labels, with kind-1 frames. The digest
is computed from the same parameter object, not supplied as a certificate.
Invalid shapes or code serialization fail before any oracle observation.
`NativeSharedLookupHelpers.completed_binding_checks` now derives that every
helper call from the actual completed lookup run passes these native binding
shape checks. Its matrices and coefficient vectors are computed by the caller.

`NativeGoldPcsPrelude` composes parameter initialization, proof-shape checks,
binding and the actual base-field random-test sampler. It accepts no prepared
geometry, bound parent or randomness certificate. Its returned `sampling`
state retains the actual sampler and computed geometry, including analysis
suspension. Rejection and suspension remain distinct. Successful finished
states have exactly `rows*width` canonical samples, with exact raw Goldilocks
conversion. The execution theorem preserves binding observations before field
sampling. Parameter initialization here represents native construction before
verification; it does not claim Rust repeats its constructor at each opening.

The fixture `/tmp/hasteboots-pcs-prelude-fixture` constructs an honest tiny
opening with two variables, width three, one left variable, one query and the
native block-RS code (message length 2, 32 blocks, block width 2). It uses the

headers, and passes the complete native PCS verifier. The Lean checks compare
its opening bytes, code-context input/digest, 18 random-test samples, exact

and the index-domain frame. Native lazy claim/evaluation words above the

## Native raw PCS weights and suffix folding

`NativeGoldMatrixAccumulate` computes the native `Matrix::add_mul` row loop
with its original accumulator. Its field projection is the previous output
plus the matrix-vector product. In particular, the one-branch fold starts
from the actual raw output of the zero-branch fold; replacing that execution
by two independently zero-initialized products can change lazy representatives.

`NativeGoldMatrixWeights` executes `matrix_weights` on raw query matrices.
The initial identity has literal raw zero/one entries, with checked-square
rejection before allocation. Each round emits all zero products before all
one products, and each later query matrix acts on the left. Valid queries
produce exactly `2^query.length` validated matrices. Every output product's
field projection, and the complete expansion's projection from identity,
are proved against the same ordered semantic expansion. Identifying this
native prefix expansion and its flattened layout with the existing semantic
Boolean-cube tensor remains a composition obligation.

`NativeGoldPackedFold` computes checked packed-table folding and evaluation,
including the native constant-lane optimization. The shortcut compares field
values via the proved canonical-word equality test, while preserving cell
zero's original words. No constant flag or semantic-table certificate is
supplied. Successful folds preserve table validity, decrement the variable
count by exactly one and retain the width. A completed checked evaluation
returns exactly that width's number of words.

`NativeGoldPackedMeaning` proves the raw fold's field interpretation. The
rectangular flattening lemma recovers each original raw cell at its native
address. The computed constant predicate proves the first cell is equal in
the field to every selected input, including inputs with different lazy
representatives. Both fold branches therefore refine the same adjacent-cell
matrix-vector operation. The complete raw loop and checked evaluation refine
the existing `FlatMatrixFold.foldAll` on the actual payload and actual query
matrices, with the least significant variable eliminated first.

`NativeGoldPcsArithmetic` copies prefix weights in lane/left-cell/source-lane
order and transposes the lane-major response without normalization. The
structured constructor's successful size is `width*(2^leftVars*width)`.
Its checked finishing wrapper exposes the native private routine's existing
constructor/query/response preconditions; it does not add a verifier
acceptance claim. `finish_value` proves that the computed suffix output is
exactly the existing flat MW-MLE fold of the original lane-major response.
`finish_length` proves its final width. Native in-place writes, allocation
behavior and Rust instruction refinement remain separate obligations.

The differential fixture `/tmp/hasteboots-pcs-arithmetic-fixture` calls the
unchanged native matrix and packed-table methods at

pairs produce `[B0*A0,B0*A1,B1*A0,B1*A1]`. The checked source hashes are

and `pcs/src/matrix_weighted.rs`:
`69b2da76d44e5abb8824bc701d7a59251709315ff1445efa06ac5e9821e74fdd`.
Other cases cover an existing lazy
accumulator, a general table, cells equal in the field but stored as different words and a table
that differs in one field lane. Native allocating and in-place folds agree

## Native Goldilocks scalar NTT and response encoding

`NativeGoldSolinas` models the canonical arithmetic used by concrete-ntt's
`PrimeModulus for Solinas` at locked revision
`cdeba793e46208320b30d78be19f7be78d49016a`. This is distinct from algebra's
lazy Goldilocks arithmetic: add/subtract return canonical words, and the
wide-product reduction retains the source's two wrapping corrections.
`reduce_spec` proves that reduction returns a canonical representative for
every 128-bit input. The field interpretation of add, subtract, reduce,
multiply and the sequential power accumulator is proved in Lean. No integer
kernel result or transform-correctness certificate is supplied as an input.

`NativeGoldNtt` supplies functional buffers for the actual scalar forward
algorithm: bit-reversed twiddle writes, canonical input conversion,
breadth-first butterfly stages and depth-first recursion above the native
1024-element threshold. The complete plan twiddle table is retained when
recursing into sub-buffers. The size proofs cover every recursion branch;
valid-stage source-pair and twiddle-address bounds are proved, including
recursive depth/half offsets. Forward outputs have exactly the original
buffer length and all raw words are canonical.

The universal correspondence between this scalar execution and the existing
`NTTButterfly`/`NTTBlockEncoder` field evaluation/code is supplied by the next
implementation layer below. Successful buffer construction alone does not
establish code membership: the actual root must be primitive and the message
coefficients must fit the chosen code degree. Root discovery, plan/cache
instantiation, the Div64 implementation, SIMD dispatch/lane operations,
mutable buffer refinement and native work-cost coupling remain open.
The scalar model preserves the real radix-two dataflow and cutoff rather
than replacing its output with a polynomial evaluator.

`NativeGoldRowEncoding` computes block-RS rows and PCS response lanes from
the original raw inputs. Its checked wrappers expose existing successful
native plan/shape preconditions; `none` represents a failed precondition,
not a claim that native assertions return a verifier `Err`. The retained
code root is compared in the field with the trusted plan root before the
zero-row shortcut. The shortcut tests literal raw zero, proved equivalent
to native canonical-and-field-zero, so lazy zero inputs take the transform
branch. The Goldilocks wrapper canonicalizes the gathered coordinate buffer
immediately before the integer kernel, without changing the original response
bytes already used by transcript binding.

The gather handles each coordinate of consecutive input blocks, a partial
final block and all zero padding. `payload_get` proves the final
symbol-major scatter contains exactly the corresponding raw coordinate
transform output. Row encoding produces `2^logSize*blockWidth` canonical
words. Response encoding independently processes every packing lane's
exact-length message chunk and concatenates lane outputs. Its completeness
and shape theorems rule out truncation under the checked preconditions.
Neither API accepts encoded responses from the proof. The code/plan
configuration is trusted input; its construction and linkage to the original
serialized native code object are not yet established.

unchanged Solinas trait/implementation and scalar forward bodies from the

## Scalar NTT-to-code correspondence

The functional canonical scalar NTT now has a universal evaluation proof and
a block-RS code-membership proof. The operational encoder is unchanged:
its original twiddle initialization, breadth/depth loops and 1024-element
cutoff still compute the returned raw words. The proof does not replace that
computation with a polynomial evaluator or accept an encoder-correctness
certificate as a protocol input.

`NativeGoldNttTwiddles` proves bit reversal reverses concatenated bit blocks,
is involutive on valid addresses and makes distinct writes non-aliasing.
The actual ordered initializer therefore puts the exact computed power in
every reversed slot. Each lookup's field value is the corresponding power
of the actual root, including the first twiddle of every recursive subtree.
These facts hold for arbitrary roots; no table-correctness premise is used.

`NativeGoldNttStages` proves contiguous-half separation for lower butterfly
stages, retaining stored-word equality. `NativeGoldNttSchedule` extends this
to all remaining breadth-first rounds and proves both complete breadth-first
execution and the actual cutoff-based depth-first execution equal one
recursive raw butterfly tree. This covers every size, including recursion
above 1024; the tree is a proof intermediary rather than a substituted
operational transform.

`NativeGoldNttMeaning.tree_value` connects each actual tree output to the
existing `NTTButterfly.transform`, with coefficients from the original
buffer and the computed full-plan table. The proof derives child roots,
subtree twiddles, source slices and output addresses. `depthFirst_value`
and `forwardData_value` lift this to complete flat output vectors, including
raw-u64 canonicalization. For a primitive root of order `2^(logSize+1)`,
`forwardData_evaluation` and the checked `forward_evaluation` API theorem
prove evaluation on the native bit-reversed odd-root domain.

`NativeGoldRowMeaning` proves coordinate gathering and all zero padding equal
the semantic coefficient table, including partially filled input blocks.
The scalar transform and original symbol-major scatter therefore compute
`BlockEncoder.encode` on that table. The raw-zero shortcut is proved to
compute the same codeword; lazy zero inputs remain on their original
transform branch. A successful encoded row lands in `BlockCode.code`, the
same whole-symbol distance code used by the opening argument. The retained
code-root version derives its agreement with the actual plan root from the
successful encoder's root check.

`NativeGoldResponseMeaning` extracts every ordered row from the actual
successful response encoder. Each comes from its original exact response
chunk, and uniform flattening preserves the native lane-major addresses.
`encodeResponses_lanes` proves that every lane of the returned flat raw
vector equals the semantic encoder of those original coefficients and is
coded. `encodeResponses_retained_lanes` states this using the original
retained code root; the required plan-root equality is derived from actual
successful checks, not supplied as a cache-consistency certificate.

The code-membership theorems require a primitive actual root, a chosen
coefficient count `m` no larger than the domain and message length at most
`m*blockWidth`. These are explicit mathematical parameter conditions, not
an assumption that the scalar transform or encoder is correct. Deriving
them from the actual native constructor/cache and linking the trusted
configuration to its serialized code object remain open. Packing-lane count,
code-symbol width and the total interleaved dimension `blockWidth*m` stay
separate.

All earlier raw native golden examples are retained. Seven added proof
instantiations check the forward API, nonconstant/partial rows, the retained
root on a zero row, and membership/coefficient linkage for arbitrary
three-lane raw responses. Two private kernel computations validate the
actual native 32/64-point root literals before applying these theorems.
All 46 new public theorems have guarded audits using only `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The combined HasteBoots suite now has
2,646 guarded audits. Default heartbeat and recursion limits are unchanged.

`NativeGoldPcsColumns.protocol` still stops at the atomic column boundary.
Next is trusted code-object linkage and composition of this computed scalar
response encoding with raw column authentication, coordinate checks and
suffix/claim equality. Actual root generation/cache behavior, Div64 and
SIMD/instruction refinement are not proved by the scalar correspondence.

extraction, production parameter/profile instantiation, strict decoding,
Rust/compiler/scheduler refinement, BabyBear, numerical certification and

## Retained block code and PCS response encoding

`NativeGoldBlockCode.Stored` retains the actual native struct fields in
serde declaration order: message length, symbol width, padded message-block
count, domain-block count, modulus string bytes and the raw domain root.
Its compositional prefix codec serializes the complete object, preserves raw
root spelling and has a proved prefix inverse and injective encoding.
`description` supplies parameter accessors and serialization from this same
object, replacing the earlier fixture-only accessor/serialized-byte pairing
in the new PCS entry point.

`build` models the native constructor arithmetic: nonzero message/symbol
width; power-of-two blowup at least two; overflow-safe ceiling division;
checked next power of two; checked domain multiplication; minimum domain 32;
and checked interleaved output size. Generation, initialization and root
loading are separate backend responses with distinct failures. The stored
root comes from the actual modeled load response. This is a functional
source model. The backend calls' implementation, mutable cache, allocation,
Rust machine operations and scheduling have not been refined into it.

`NativeGoldBlockCodeMeaning` proves ceiling coverage/minimality, least
power-of-two padding, the exact domain exponent and strict expansion.
Constructor success therefore derives the coefficient count and all padding
and output-size inequalities required by the scalar correspondence. The
Brakedown code-shape gate follows when the constructor message length matches
the native left/right split; no independently chosen coefficient count or
code-shape certificate is needed.

`primitive_log_upper` proves that a Goldilocks primitive root for degree
`2^(logSize+1)` forces `logSize <= 31`, since `2^33` does not divide `p-1`.
With a primitive retained root, the constructor's own loaded backend derives
root agreement and every scalar encoder precondition. Exact-size response
encoding is consequently total. `response_lanes` connects every returned
lane to the original response chunk and `BlockCode.code` at the constructor's
own `messageBlocks`, removing the earlier free degree/padding premises.
Root primitivity is still an explicit mathematical backend obligation;
it has not been derived from concrete-ntt's repeated-square-root discovery.

`NativeGoldBlockCodeContext` computes the complete native parameter metadata
and hash input from the retained object. Structural injectivity of that input
recovers all parameter fields and the complete stored code, including the
padded coefficient count, modulus bytes and raw root. This is injectivity of
hash inputs, not a claim that hash outputs are collision-free. The structural
prefix readers are not a strict adversarial Rust decoder refinement.

`NativeGoldPcsEncoding.protocol` continues the original checked single-opening
PCS prefix through response encoding after the distinct column count check.
The exact same retained object supplies context bytes and encoding geometry.
A loaded plan root is obtained from the backend; both response vectors are
computed by the original scalar encoder, never passed in as certificates.
The prior random state, structured weights, sampled indices and observation
trace are preserved. Loading/encoding unavailability models the native trusted
cache/assertion boundary separately from verifier rejection or analysis
suspension. The functional backend response is shared at the retained size;
concurrent mutation and individual native cache calls are not refined here.

`columns_complete` derives both response shapes from the actual checked
prefix and proves response encoding succeeds for the constructed code with
its own primitive backend root. `encoded_coded` proves both actual output
vectors are coded and have coefficients from their original exact chunks.
This is an encoding boundary, not PCS acceptance. Column authentication,
coordinate checks and final suffix/claim equality remain to be composed.

## Raw column workers and checked PCS preparation

`NativeGoldColumnChecks` computes the original lane/coordinate loop from raw
Goldilocks words. Products and ascending left-to-right accumulation use the
verified lazy u64 arithmetic; equality compares canonical field values, as
native Goldilocks comparison does. Every dot product is proved equal to its
semantic row sum and to the existing `NativeColumnLayout.dot`. The complete
boolean loop is equivalent to both coordinate equation families. Native
indexing preconditions are explicit as `Shape`; `addresses` proves every
weight, payload and encoded-response access is in bounds under that shape.
Optional getters totalize the source model outside these preconditions; they
are not used to justify accepting malformed arrays.

`NativeGoldColumnWorker` hashes the original received `Row`, parses its
leaf-first path, checks the native sibling chain, and computes coordinate
checks only after authentication succeeds. Its hash-only VCVio computation
compiles to the same mixed-oracle native authentication/coordinate program.
The shared hash encoding is the existing injective raw-row encoding. No
semantic field list is serialized in place of the raw payload; distinct lazy
representatives remain distinct hash inputs.

The raw workers instantiate the existing `HashWorkerPool`. Arbitrary
individual hash advances, interleaving, shared scheduler work, cancellation
and retained earlier calls are covered by that pool's operational theorem.
Its computed final all-accepted flag derives replay of every original raw
payload/path and the actual coordinate flag from the final shared cache.
`NativeGoldPcsWorkerSoundness.accepted_checks` turns those flags into both
semantic coordinate families. It does not take supplied worker traces or
external Merkle-acceptance/replay certificates.

`NativeGoldPcsWorkers.protocol` continues the actual retained-code PCS
encoding entry point into prepared worker inputs. It preserves every earlier
rejection, suspension and backend-unavailability outcome. Recursive pairing
requires both lists to end together; its projections recover the complete
ordered received columns and sampled indices. The preceding actual distinct
count check proves this pairing succeeds. Preparation retains the computed
random/structured weights, both computed encoded vectors, original root,
geometry, packing width and resulting atomic transcript for later steps.
It emits no additional oracle observations and is not an acceptance result.

`prepared_shape` derives every worker's array preconditions from the actual
checked prefix and retained block-code constructor. It uses the original
received-column shape checks, actual bounded sampled indices, computed
random/structured matrix sizes and actual response-encoder output lengths.
There is no caller-provided geometry or response-shape certificate in the
entry point. Packing width and code-symbol width remain separate.

The mixed-oracle prefix and probabilistic shared-cache pool still have
separate execution interfaces. Their checkpoint/observation-state coupling,
native Rayon scheduling/completion refinement and a full PCS acceptance
entry point are not established by these local worker theorems. In
particular this does not yet connect authenticated raw payloads to the
prefix-frozen semantic word used by proximity analysis. Final suffix/claim
enforcement and full lookup/helper PCS composition remain open.
