## Raw frozen-word availability and pool loss

`NativeGoldPcsPaths.prepared_paths` derives every prepared job's typed Merkle
position and exact leaf-first path length from the actual checked PCS prefix.
It uses the original column/path guards, bounded sampled indices and computed
Merkle height. This part needs neither primitive-root correctness nor a
caller-supplied path/geometry certificate.

`NativeGoldRawRequests.fromJob` computes the typed availability request from
the original job: its sampled index, original raw `Row`, retained root and
parsed leaf/siblings. The context tag and height family identify the trusted
checkpoint configuration. Out-of-range positions or incorrect path lengths
return `none`. `entries` requires every original job to convert successfully;
it retains each job alongside its request and never drops, truncates or merges
a worker, even when two positions coincide. Its proved first projection is
the entire original job list, and every second component is its actual
computed request. `replay_of_worker` transfers replay from the literal raw
worker computation to the generic raw-payload availability interface.

`NativeGoldRawAvailability.frozenRaw` selects the immutable total raw word
from a recorded checkpoint's cumulative prefix log and root, with an empty
raw-row fallback. Only after that selection do `frozenValue`/`frozenWord`
interpret coordinates in Goldilocks, with zero for missing coordinates.
The frozen object depends on the checkpoint and trusted layout dimensions;
it has no later query, response, worker-result or challenge input. Placing
the actual native checkpoint before the opening challenges remains part of
the state-coupling obligation. This is the information-theoretic prefix
resolver, not an efficient decoder claim.

Outside the existing `ParallelColumnAvailability.Failure` event, an accepted
raw request equals this frozen raw payload. Field-value projection therefore
preserves the original native coordinate equations against the same frozen
word. Both random and structured response families use one conjunction of
equations. No projected field list is substituted into a hash input, and no
injectivity of Goldilocks value projection is assumed (it is false for lazy
aliases). Missing/unavailable payloads and malformed unqueried raw lengths
still give a total semantic word; native queried lengths remain established
by the earlier checked-prefix array-bound theorem.

`NativeGoldPcsRawAvailability.prepare` applies that lossless adapter to an
actual prepared PCS result. Its completeness theorem derives all request
preconditions from the checked prefix when the trusted context height matches
the computed native height. Actual pool acceptance then derives raw replay
and the coordinate checks for every computed request from the final shared
cache, without incoming replay/acceptance certificates. `pool_equations`
transports those checks to every recorded matching root's frozen semantic
word outside the same joint availability event.

`NativeGoldRawAvailability.failure_le_charge` and its empty-initialization
version reduce failed semantic transport to the existing joint root-wide
hash hazard for arbitrary adaptive programs returning request views.
`NativeGoldPcsRawFailure.failure_le_charge` additionally specializes this
reduction to the actual worker-pool computation: the event requires its
computed all-accepted residual-worker flag, yet the frozen equations fail.
The reduction uses support of that actual pool run, not arbitrary fabricated
pool outputs. All original scheduler work, interleaving, cancellation and
issued hashes stay in the charged program. No per-worker, per-lane,
per-coordinate or extra response-family union factor is introduced. This is
a symbolic expected-hazard bound, not the final numerical security claim.

`NativeGoldPcsDraws.typed` checks both the exact original quota length and all

entire original list; `typed_complete` proves conversion succeeds when the
existing native request bounds hold. Malformed lengths or positions return
`none`, rather than truncating or substituting a fallback draw.

`prepared_sample` extracts the original actual atomic-request result from the
checked PCS execution. The full request equation includes the actual
response-bound transcript and the original native label/domain/quota.
Prepared job indices equal its sorted/deduplicated indices, but its ordered
draw list still has the original query quota. Every draw, including each
repeat, is bounded by the computed Merkle domain and covered by an unchanged
prepared job. The resulting transcript is retained. `prepared_typed` derives
the typed original vector and this coverage directly from execution success.
These results identify samples; they do not assume or establish fresh
uniform production challenges.

`NativeGoldPcsAgrees.pool_position` transports the existing raw-pool equations
to a fixed recorded checkpoint at any covered position. It recovers the

not replace the query quota by the number of distinct received columns.

`NativeGoldPcsOpeningChecks.prepared_parameters` derives that geometry is the

`prepared_agrees` combines actual checked-prefix success, the original atomic

## Computed PCS completion and suffix claims

`NativeGoldPcsClaim.verify` computes the native suffix fold from the original
unencoded `opening.evaluation` and compares the result with the original raw
claimed row using Goldilocks field equality. It does not compare serialized
words or take a supplied finished vector. `equal_iff`, `accepted_iff` and
`accepted_value` connect the executable check to the semantic suffix equation.
The prefix continues to bind the original serialized claim without replacing
it by its canonical representative.

`NativeGoldPcsFinishComplete` proves completeness of the raw packed fold loop,
its evaluator and the PCS suffix wrapper. `prepared_finish` derives all
matrix validation, query/response dimensions, nonzero width and allocation
bounds from the actual completed checked prefix. Consequently
`prepared_no_finish_error` rules out the defensive suffix-shape failure on
that prefix; a wrong final claim can still be rejected.

`NativeGoldPcsAcceptance.program` maps the existing general interleaved worker
pool to a computed completion status. Acceptance requires that every residual
worker has actually returned true, followed by a successful suffix/claim
check. A returned false worker rejects columns; an unfinished pool is an
analysis suspension. The latter is not a native verifier error. The scheduler
cannot supply an acceptance flag. `failed_iff` and `anyRejected_iff` identify
rejection with actual false-returning residual programs.

`program_origin` and `accepted_origin` retain the original pool result,
scheduler memory and shared final state/cache, with no additional oracle
queries. `NativeGoldPcsAcceptanceSoundness.accepted_workers` derives raw
payload/path replay and both native coordinate checks for every original job
from this supported accepted execution. `accepted_value` additionally uses
the actual checked prefix to derive the semantic final claim equation. The
statement deliberately retains separate checked-prefix and supported-pool
execution premises: coupling these interfaces into one native transcript and
checkpoint/cache execution remains required.

`supported_replay` proves that every supported compiled prefix equals the

`NativeGoldPcsExecution.program` compiles the actual checked parameter,

`completed_origin` obtains the real intermediate state and both supported

`NativeGoldPcsExecutionAgrees.accepted_agrees` connects this same run to both

## Source checkpoints before native lookup challenges

`NativeHashPrefix.HashOnly` excludes SHAKE starts and reads on every adaptive
hash-answer branch. Its bind closure and native-log theorem retain all hash
observations. `compile_independent` proves that changing the complete reader
backend leaves the compiled hash-only program unchanged. This is a structural
statement conditional on the same inputs and preceding state, not a new
probability or transcript-input freshness assumption.

`NativeSharedLookupHashPrefix` establishes this property for the actual
context computation, selected-source contexts, framing, numeric preflight
steps/loop, complete registry registration and parent preparation. All
failure branches are included. Thus the actual parent metadata processing
and all original registry context hashes precede the child/outer lookup
challenge stage, rather than using a late checkpoint before PCS randomness.

`NativeCheckpointBoundary` executes a compiled native stage, records its
computed root family using the existing passive `RecordRoots` operation,
then executes the native continuation in the same shared state. Its origin
lemmas recover the actual intermediate states. Every snapshot uses the same
actual pre-recording hash log; recording preserves the hash cache/log/keys.
`native_replay` proves exact erasure of the ghost annotations, including the
whole original native value and ordered observation list. `program_recorded`
retains each snapshot through the complete continuation without conditioning
on acceptance, collision freedom or an unset stability monitor.

`NativeSharedLookupCheckpoints` factors the original complete shared lookup
entry point into parent preparation followed by its existing child launcher
and scalar/terminal/finish body. `native_eq` proves equality of the native
programs themselves. The wrapper records every original registry slot after
successful preparation and before that continuation. Failed preparation
records no roots and retains its actual partial hash work. Root selection
uses the original ordered registry, independently of which slots later open.
It includes unused slots and unused earlier aliases of a later used source.
A configuration-tag embedding permits the same shared state to contain later
helper checkpoints with different trusted shapes. No slot is truncated,
sorted or deduplicated by this layer.

`freeze_independent` proves the complete preparation/recording computation is
unchanged by the reader supplying the later lookup challenges. `native_replay`
recovers the complete original lookup entry point from the final shared cache.
`recorded_sources` derives successful parent preparation and actual earlier,
recorded and final states from one supported run returning a body result.
Every original source root has a snapshot of that earlier prefix log in both
the pre-child state and the final state. The caller supplies no independent
prepared transcript, successful parent prefix or checkpoint-membership proof.
Existing checkpoint-history lemmas retain these same snapshots through
subsequent PCS/scheduler work.

The existing native parent fixture now checks unchanged context hashes and

alias of slot two; all three roots are recorded in original order. Changing

original native observation and all hashes plus the passive source record.

## Persistent SHAKE cache and lazy native programs

`NativeShakeCache` owns a persistent cache keyed by the complete SHAKE input
and byte offset. A hit returns the saved byte without an oracle request;
a miss consumes one private uniform byte and installs its answer. No reader
identity occurs in the key. Every possible read preserves all previously
exposed answers and records its entire returned interval in the final cache.
Consequently, rereading an interval returns exactly the same bytes without
new randomness. Splitting a read preserves byte order and the complete cache.
These laws apply to arbitrary initial caches, including partial overlaps.

`NativeLazyProgram.compile` executes the original causal native program in
this cache state over the existing shared checkpoint specification. All
SHA-512 requests still use that specification's canonical hash interface.
The compiler retains every ordered native observation, including repeated
reads and hash calls. Native continuations receive only their returned
answer; they cannot supply or replace the cache. Composition threads one
cache through both programs, and every possible compiled branch preserves
previously exposed bytes.

`NativeProgramPrefix.take` retains the actual residual program at an analysis
boundary. Its world semantics is the existing `OracleProgram.runPrefix`.
Binding the residual continuation reconstructs the original program exactly.
`NativeLazyProgram.compile_resume` transports that identity to the stateful
interpreter, including both observation lists and the persistent cache.
Thus analysis fuel does not impose a native retry limit or refresh challenges.

## Native prequery-aware index laws

`NativePrequeryIndexLaw` proves the actual native atomic-index phase's exact
conditional law after the entire mixed SHAKE/SHA-512 history. It retains the
old byte on every previously exposed coordinate and samples only the unseen
coordinates. This covers partial reads, overlapping and cloned readers,
off-path queries, and request inputs selected after prequerying them. It
conditions on the complete prior result and ordered log, rather than success
or a purported first verifier visit. The product-world sigma algebra is
unchanged; no full-reader conditioning or zero-probability fiber is used.

The native decoder transports that masked byte law to the complete ordered
draw vector. The usual Hamming-agreement probability is recovered only under
an explicit disjointness premise for every byte in the requested block.
Complete overlap instead yields a deterministic vector, including on the
verifier's first visit. A separate law preserves the native ordered list,
without reducing the quota when equal positions occur.

The native request theorem includes its entire `Option Result`, updated
transcript, sorted/deduplicated transport indices and both native observations.
Adaptive request parameters—including transcript, label, domain and original
quota—and the tested predicate may be selected from the whole prior result
and log. The unnormalized law retains that history's exact mass, without a
success floor or query cutoff. Validity is required only for the selected
request on the analyzed history, not for unrelated histories.

`NativeGoldPrequeryIndices` identifies the checked Goldilocks PCS draw adapter
with the original literal draw vector. Its conditional event law consequently
uses the same cache-masked generator. Successful parsing and transport
deduplication introduce no new independence or freshness assumption.

Twelve new public theorems have guarded axiom audits using only `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Kernel regressions include retained and
fresh bytes in one block, complete-input separation, cloned observations,
prequeries to discarded high bytes, duplicate draws versus unique transport
indices, complete prior exposure and a native framed request selected after
its complete input was prequeried. The last case remains determined by the
old bytes even when the fresh generator supplies different bytes.

This establishes the native atomic-index conditional law in the joint-world
model. Finite-prefix distributional equivalence of `NativeLazyProgram` to
that world, the first-exposure ledger, early root freezing and parent/child
guessing exceptions remain open. The scheduler and checkpoint compilers
still require lazy-cache integration. Rectangular PCS bounds, full native
batch composition, application extraction, concrete work realization,
production profile certificates and the final 128-bit theorem remain open,
as do the native refinement and BabyBear gates. The full goal remains active.

## Rectangular proximity and shared-column opening

`ModuleCodeProximity` separates the scalar field used for test coins from the
module used for whole code symbols. It generalizes the pinned ArkLib AHIV22
affine-line and row-span argument, retaining its Apache 2.0 attribution. The
module proves common-support alignment for sparse subspaces, a far direction
in the source-row span, affine-line counting and the uniform coefficient law.
The scalar-field-size premise `radius < |F|` is explicit, along with
`3 * radius < minimum distance`; no small-field alignment exception is omitted.
Dependent source rows are allowed through proved uniform fibers.

For minimum distance `delta` and `testWidth` independent base-field rows, the
proved proximity term is `(delta / |F|)^testWidth`. The alphabet may be
`Fin codeWidth → F` with no equality between `codeWidth` and `testWidth`.
This is the conservative repeated-row bound, not an assumed extension of the
older square bound `delta / |F|^testWidth`. The two expressions are not
interchangeable. No numeric production security level follows yet.

`RectangularBaseProximity` specializes that law to the existing semantic
`BlockCode`, `StructuredOpening.combine` and the common-source decoder's
complete-column metric. Every column includes all source rows and all symbol
coordinates. Its explicit-distance corollary uses the existing checked
`BlockCode.minDist` theorem and retains independent test and code widths.

`RectangularOpening` now composes the far and near branches for a fixed
available word. Malicious coded responses may depend on the preceding random
matrix. The encoded far-branch corollary derives their code membership from
their coefficient arrays using `BlockEncoder.encode_mem_code`. Every response
uses the same ordered column vector. The near/far column terms are combined
by a maximum; shared column acceptance probabilities are not multiplied.
All structured queries use one total common decoder for that available word.

There are eighteen new public production theorems, each with a guarded axiom
audit using only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The focused
suite supplies an inhabited width-3/code-width-4 example over `ZMod 5` with
proved code distance 2 and a far word. A second example instantiates the actual
semantic `BlockCode` bridge at those unequal widths, deriving the distance and
common-source far premise. Honest encoded zero responses accept for every
matrix and shared draw. A separate regression proves that three identical
checks sharing one column draw accept with probability `1/2`, rather than a
product of three independent column probabilities.

This closes the rectangular fixed-word proximity and shared-column interactive
opening interface. It does not yet connect rectangular response finishing to
the native matrix query, instantiate the retained native constructor and all
production roles, or certify numeric 128-bit feasibility. Global first-exposure
Fiat–Shamir causality, the lazy/world distribution bridge, native batch and
helper composition, application extraction and concrete attacker-work
realization remain open, together with native refinement and BabyBear. The
full security goal remains active.

## Lazy SHAKE read law and native index execution

`NativeShakeKernel` identifies the physical cached-or-uniform byte sampler
with the joint world's exact conditional byte law after the entire mixed
SHAKE/SHA-512 past. Its initial cache comes from that finite observed footprint.
The kernel transports arbitrary byte predicates and predicates on the returned
byte plus updated cache. The actual shared interpreter step leaves every
SHA-512/checkpoint field unchanged. A prior observation of SHA-512 on the same
input does not populate a SHAKE coordinate.

`NativeShakeHistory` reconstructs the exact byte-cache effect of every supported
read and compiled program from the complete retained observation list. Hits,
repeated reads and partial overlaps remain in that list. The same property
holds after any typed shared oracle implementation, using proved support
inclusion rather than an external cache-coherence certificate.

`NativeShakeReadLaw` extends the physical byte step to a whole read. Its
actual shared execution preserves the entire shared state and uses the
private cached sampler. The sampler has exactly the eager finite-vector
masked law, including its final byte cache. This is an equality of probability
laws: the eager generator's unused coins at cached coordinates are analytical
and are not charged as native work. Output order, interval writes and every
previously exposed answer are retained. The final event theorem compares the
joint world's whole-history conditional read with the actual shared execution,
including both states and allowing arbitrary partial overlap. No fresh-block,
first-reader, or successful-verification premise is used.

`NativeLazyIndexExecution` applies that read law to the actual checked native
atomic-index program, compiled by `NativeLazyProgram`. It proves equality of
the complete native result, updated transcript, ordered observation list,
owned byte cache and shared hash/checkpoint state under the full conditional
past. Native framing and decoding coincide with the earlier finite-vector
index law. Invalid dimensions return before drawing bytes and preserve both
prior interpreter states. Sorting and transport deduplication leave the
original with-replacement draw quota intact.

All twenty-six new public lemmas have guarded axiom audits using only
`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Thirty focused regressions cover
an actual mixed read/hash history, namespace separation, input separation,
partial/cached/empty reads, cache reconstruction, physical zero-query cache
hits, native framed partial prequeries, ordered duplicates versus unique
transport indices, and invalid native dimensions.

This completes a conditional distribution bridge for a real native atomic-index
phase and its physical lazy read. It does not yet prove the general mixed
program's finite-prefix distribution law from empty interpreter states, nor
integrate the worker scheduler and source/helper checkpoint compiler. In
particular, cache reconstruction alone is not the probability theorem.
First-exposure root freezing, parent/child guessing exceptions, rectangular
matrix finishing and actual batch/helper PCS composition remain open, followed
by full application extraction, numeric profiles, concrete attacker-work
realization and the final 128-bit expected-work theorem. Native refinement
and BabyBear remain separate required gates. The full goal stays active.

## Conditional mixed-program execution and final byte cache

`NativeLazyExecutionLaw.execute_law` proves exact conditional event probability
for **the actual `NativeLazyProgram.compile` interpreter** under the shared
`CheckpointExecution.handler`, against the original joint product world.
The event may inspect the arbitrary result and complete ordered native log.
The initial history is any replayable execution, including prequeries; its
observed SHAKE cache and projected SHA-512 cache supply the interpreter state.
Read lengths, offsets, inputs and subsequent read/hash instructions may depend
on preceding responses. Repeated inputs, partial overlaps, reader restarts,
zero-length reads and cached hashes require no disjointness premise.

The proof has these independently checked layers:

- `OracleHistoryComposition`: exact total probability over the countable range
  of complete replayable histories, for any finite measure, then exact
  refinement inside an earlier history conditional. Zero-mass refined fibers
  remain in the partition; no successful-execution normalization is used.
- `OracleHistorySnapshot`: retain the whole prior result/log and the actual
  next response in the analysis payload. Later fibers fix both the earlier
  history and the response without adding oracle observations.
- `NativeShakeProjection`: a truthful log fold reconstructs the observed byte
  cache; appending a read updates precisely its interval, while starts and
  hashes leave the SHAKE cache unchanged. A whole-history fiber fixes this
  cache even when other coordinates remain unknown.
- `OracleKernelComposition`: exact score and arbitrary-continuation transfer
  for physical SHAKE sampling and canonical cached SHA-512 answers, using the
  whole-history posterior and exact history-refinement averaging.
- `NativeLazyExecution`: literal code equalities for pure/start/read/hash
  execution, including the canonical hash-state and passive-monitor update.
  `executeWithCache_records` derives the owned final SHAKE cache from supported
  executions of that actual handler and the retained complete log.
- `NativeLazyExecutionLaw`: structural induction over mixed programs combines
  those laws. `prefix_law` retains the actual residual program, `from_empty`
  discharges both initial-cache premises, and `cache_law` extends the exact
  event equality to the owned final byte cache of the old-plus-new history.

This closes the general finite-program and finite-analysis-prefix
**value/log/SHAKE-cache probability bridge**, beyond the prior one-request laws.
It does not yet assert equality of all final shared monitor/checkpoint states,
an infinite sampler completion theorem, native Rust refinement, or complete
Fiat–Shamir/application security. The syntax is a causal well-founded program;
unbounded retry processes still need compatible prefix families and limits.

The next Gate A obligations are final SHA-512/monitor state recovery and
compatible-prefix limits, followed by the first-exposure ledger and earliest
relevant-byte root freezing across raw/off-path/descendant prequeries. Gate B
still needs rectangular native finishing and constructor instantiation, then
an inhabited numerical Goldilocks profile and query-feasibility certificate.
The final work theorem, BabyBear profile and fail-closed Rust refinement remain
mandatory. No verifier-work substitution or query cutoff is introduced here.

## Full shared-state execution and causal lifetime limits

`NativeLazyStateExecution.state_law` extends the exact mixed-program
probability bridge to **the entire actual compiled outcome**: arbitrary result,
complete native log, owned SHAKE cache, canonical SHA-512 cache, checkpoint
registry and passive failure flag. The implementation is the existing
`simulateQ CheckpointExecution.handler ((NativeLazyProgram.compile p).run cache)`
with both state layers retained, rather than a replacement oracle interpreter.
Supported executions reconstruct both state layers from the literal ordered
log; this gives an equality of actual `ProbComp` computations before applying
the conditional event law. `fold_project` identifies the final shared hash
state with the canonical projection of the old-plus-new native log.

The shared-state fold applies the actual `afterHash` update on every hash,
including cached repeats. It retains a failure detected before later queries
repair source stability. Starts and reads leave the shared state unchanged.
This program syntax issues no checkpoint-registration query, so it preserves
the **initial** registry; this theorem does not insert or relocate native root
registration. `prefix_law` retains the residual program and every state field,
and `from_empty` discharges the initial-history premises.

`OracleMachine` supplies a causal interface for truly unbounded retry loops.
A local state chooses a done/start/read/hash command; response continuations
receive only the corresponding response. Local state can include the entire
attacker memory and an initially chosen random tape. Finite `take` prefixes
return the real residual local state or completed result. They do not impose
a runtime retry limit. The syntax permits machines with no terminating run.

`take_resume` proves exact prefix compatibility. `compile_resume` carries the
owned byte cache, and `execute_resume` carries **both caches and the complete
shared state** across suspension. Thus longer prefixes use the actual cached
execution, with no independent rerun of already sampled bytes. Their ideal
logs extend by prefix. Completed results/logs are absorbing at all later fuel.

`conditional_lifetime_law` proves that the probability of ever seeing a
persistent bad-log event equals the supremum of the actual full-state prefix
probabilities after any replayable prequery history. `lifetime_law` starts from
empty caches. `completion_lifetime_law` gives the corresponding exact limit
for bad completed results, with no termination assumption, query cutoff,
success floor or conditioning on successful completion. `eventual_measurable`
proves measurability of arbitrary eventual prefix-result events in the original
joint product sigma algebra. These are lifetime **event-probability** limits;
no claim about a general infinite-trace distribution or almost-sure termination
is needed or made.

Gate A now has a full-state finite-prefix bridge and compatible causal
lifetime-event limits. Its next substantive obligation is the first-exposure
ledger and earliest relevant-byte root freezing, including raw/off-path and
descendant prequeries, followed by native phase/registration composition.
The attacker-work coupling, rectangular native finishing/constructor and
numerical-profile gates, final application/extraction theorem, BabyBear and
fail-closed Rust/scheduler refinement remain open.

## Raw first-seed exposure and cache-aware guessing risk

`OracleFirstExposure` finds the earliest returned-coordinate exposure directly
in the complete raw native observation log. Its minimality certificate splits
that **same** log into the earlier history, first relevant observation and
suffix; every earlier coordinate set is disjoint from the relevant set. Starts,
empty reads and SHA-512 coordinates cannot expose SHAKE bytes. Complete input
bytes and offsets identify cells, so clones/restarts share exposure while
prefix-related but unequal inputs do not. Appending observations cannot move
an existing first exposure. Arbitrary, unclassified, duplicate and rejected
queries remain in the original ordered log; this index is not a work metric.

The seed specialization includes all 64 coordinates of a native parent seed
under its exact complete SHAKE input. It detects a first read at any seed
position, rather than assuming a verifier read or offset zero came first.
`OracleMachineExposure.log_take` identifies log truncation with an actual
causal-machine analysis prefix. `pre_exposure_fresh` therefore gives a replayable
**actual** pre-exposure history with all 64 seed coordinates unseen.
`pre_exposure_targets` derives exact fixed-target hit probability
`targets.card / 2^512` under that complete-history conditional.

`OracleMaskCounting` separately counts full raw-mask fibers. A target
inconsistent with any known byte has no fiber. Each compatible target has
exactly `256^known.card` raw responses, and distinct targets have disjoint
fibers. Cancellation gives the exact masked uniform target-hit probability:

```
compatible_target_count / 256^(coordinate_count - known_coordinate_count)
```

`OracleSeedGuessing.target_law` transfers this count to the whole-history SHAKE
posterior, retaining arbitrary partial overlap and mixed prequeries. Its
`risk_read_average` and `risk_hash_average` prove exact conditional averaging
across an actual later read or shared hash query. A partial read can increase
or decrease the pointwise completion risk; only its conditional average is
preserved. No per-byte `2^-512` claim is made. `fresh_seed_targets` uses the full
`2^512` denominator only with the explicit all-64-unseen premise.

These results supply the earliest-seed-exposure and orphan-guessing
probability primitives. **They do not yet freeze native roots.** The next
required bridge must parse complete raw native inputs, extract context/root
keys and quoted parent seeds, retain orphan descendant queries, prove that
the target set and next request are selected from the prior history, and
place proof-only availability registrations before the first relevant
response. In particular, a target set chosen using future seed bytes cannot
be substituted into the fixed-target theorem. Native root/context classifier
completeness, parent-child guessing exceptions, protocol composition and real
attacker-work coupling remain open, along with the other application and
native-refinement gates.

## Native raw-input root and parent-seed views

`NativeExactCodec` turns existing structural prefix codecs into exact input
views: recognition requires an empty trailing suffix and byte-for-byte
canonical reencoding. `read_iff` proves that recognizing a value is equivalent
to the input being its exact encoding. This is an analysis parser; it does not
replace or refine the native adversarial proof deserializer.

`NativeChildSeedView` reads the fixed sixth frame (index 5) of a **complete**
raw framed input. It recognizes the immediate-parent-seed label only there,
with exactly the canonical 64-byte digest payload. A forged later frame with
the same label does not add or replace the candidate. Soundness identifies the
actual decoded frame and exact bytes. Completeness is proved against the real
`NativeTranscript.forkChild` output, with the native frame-length bounds.
A `HasHeader` invariant preserves that seed through any valid absorption,
byte-challenge request and field-reader request, including zero-length field
requests. The unframed consumed-field-byte receipt domain is explicitly
rejected by this framed view; its raw observations remain in the execution.

The collector takes at most one quoted candidate per nonempty raw output or
hash observation, retains repeated observations in the underlying log, and
deduplicates only the guessed-seed target set. Its cardinality is at most the
actual raw observation count. `orphan_probability` combines this native
collector with the earlier first-exposure law: the event of the logical
parent seed matching a candidate parsed from the **actual prior machine log**
has exact probability `candidate_count / 2^512`. The target set is fixed by
conditioning on the complete prior result/log, rather than chosen using later
seed bytes. The all-64-unseen premise comes from the actual pre-exposure
prefix. This count is not an attacker-work certificate and includes no claim
that verifier queries can be charged to the attacker.

`NativeRootInputView` recognizes context/root source vectors in the actual
Goldilocks canonical-bind and deferred-registry encodings. Its binding reader
checks the serialized extension degree 3, helper context and full source
vector. Exact canonical guards reject trailing or altered payloads. Single
PCS openings recognize the adjacent native row-code-context and
commitment/query frames using the complete opening codec. Complete raw input
views first decode the entire framed stream, then retain ordered mentions.
Recognition is proved for the actual `registry`, `bind` and
`NativeGoldPcsBinding.appendBound` functions. Original source vectors survive
as ordered sublists, retaining repetitions and unused entries. Adjacent single
opening pairs remain present after any earlier frame prefix.

The mention list is **not** the native opening registry or its first-original
representative map. Flattening mentions must not substitute a first-mentioned
alias for the native first original registry slot. The exact decoded frames
and registry vector remain the authoritative evidence for that later bridge.
The views also do not establish that a parsed context digest names trusted
parameters, that a quoted seed authenticates parent ownership, or that a
mentioned root has an available word.

Next, associate parsed descendants and helper roots with their actual parent
contexts, prove causal selection of the parent request from the prior machine
state, and insert availability snapshots before the first relevant raw
response while proving erasure to the actual interpreter. Receipt-linked
future prefixes need their own guessing/freshness argument; a guessed consumed
field block does not automatically have 512 bits of entropy. Native first-slot
alias/group order, full protocol composition, attacker-work coupling and the
remaining rectangular/numerical/application/refinement gates stay open.

## Causally selected seed exposures and online direct-root snapshots

`CausalSeedExposure` selects the pending native request from the actual local
machine state retained by a replayable prefix. An eligible first read is
nonempty, intersects positions 0–63, and has no earlier exposure of any of the
64 logical seed coordinates. Both its complete input and the guessed-seed set
parsed from the prior raw log are fixed on the complete history fiber. The
exact conditional event probability is therefore `prior_candidate_count /
2^512`, with no selection of a request input from later witness data.
`event_measurable` and `averaged_event` prove measurability and exact averaging
over the actual countable range of complete histories; no measurable local
state or payload assumption is added. This event concerns a **new** first
exposure. It does not reset inherited bad risk or assign 512 bits of entropy
to receipt guesses or partially exposed seeds.

`NativeDirectRootFreeze` now instruments the **actual owned-cache lazy
compiler**, rather than only recording roots at a verifier phase boundary.
For each nonempty raw read, it parses the complete input with
`NativeRootInputView`, removes duplicate context/root keys and those already
present in earlier nonempty read observations, and issues `RecordRoots`
checkpoint annotations before the byte read. Context digests are the ghost
configuration tags; an application must still prove their trusted shape and
parameter interpretation. Empty reads keep their original native observation
but record no root. Starts and shared hash calls remain in the complete
history; neither is silently charged as a SHAKE exposure.

The operational guarantees are proved as follows:

- `erase_compile` erases only checkpoint requests and recovers the original
  `NativeLazyProgram.compile` computation, retaining its complete result/log,
  owned SHAKE cache, and literal private/hash queries.
- `canonical_compile` and `execute_erasure` reuse the existing canonical
  checkpoint-erasure theorem. Under the actual shared handler, result/log,
  owned byte cache and shared hash cache agree exactly with the original
  execution. The proof-only registry and failure monitor intentionally differ.
- `execute_read` identifies the root state recorded from the actual pre-read
  cumulative hash log before the private byte sampler. `read_snapshot` proves
  that every supported continuation retains that exact checkpoint, without
  assuming monitor success, collision freedom or a query bound.
- `fresh_after_output` prevents a cloned read of the same input from recording
  the keys again. Key identity is the complete `(context digest,root)` pair;
  equal roots under different contexts remain distinct.
- `compile_bind` and `compile_resume` thread the real ordered history and the
  same owned byte cache through composition and finite-prefix suspension.
  A suspension does not refresh root snapshots or challenge bytes.

These guarantees apply to directly parsed source mentions. They do **not**
yet cover helper-root frames lacking their parent helper context, associate
orphan descendants with parents, or establish availability of every root used
by an accepted verifier run. Earliest-exposure application requires the initial
history, owned byte cache and prior checkpoints to come from the same
instrumented prelude (or the empty initial state). Passing a historical log
alone is not a certificate that its earlier roots were registered. Similarly,
the flat mention order does not replace the native first-original-slot alias
map or ordered-prefix query grouping.

Next, retain compatible pending-parent contexts during partial seed reads,
use those contexts to register helper roots before their equality challenges,
and prove the whole native root/exposure coverage statement with explicit
orphan/receipt exceptions. Then compose source availability and arithmetic
with the real attacker-work ledger; raw log cardinality is not substituted for
attacker cost, and no verifier/setup work is charged to the attacker. The
remaining rectangular/numerical/application and fail-closed refinement gates
remain mandatory.

## Partial-parent association and causal helper-root snapshots

`NativeParentInputView` recognizes the actual native parent-seed request
(kind 6 fork followed by the kind 2, 64-byte classical-child-seed request),
canonical helper contexts in bind messages, and canonical helper-root
vectors. `parseParent_request` links recognition to
`NativeTranscript.requestInput (absorb parent 6 label context) ... 64`.
Compatibility inspects only already observed positions of the seed, and
`compatible_observed` proves that the actual logical seed remains compatible
after arbitrary partial reads. A single unknown final byte retains all 256
possible values.

`NativeParentLedger` stores every compatible pending parent, its resolved
source keys and its inherited helper contexts. A child header can resolve
helper roots against several compatible parents; the resolver does not pick
the first seed match or require a complete seed read. Stored metadata also
allows source/context propagation into later descendants. Discovery uses the
old parent table and old byte cache. Its frozen set is unchanged: a parent
discovered after an earlier child read cannot backdate that read's snapshot.
Only preparation for a subsequent nonempty read adds resolved keys to the
persistent frozen set. Duplicate keys are removed, complete context/root
pairs remain distinct, existing parents are retained, and previously frozen
keys are never requested again.

`NativeParentRootFreeze` threads this ledger through the actual owned-cache
compiler. Starts, hashes and empty reads may discover parent structure;
nonempty reads issue newly resolved root checkpoints before reading any
bytes. The compiler never supplies its ghost state to the native continuation.
`erase_compile`, `canonical_compile` and `execute_erasure` prove exact
projection to the original native value/log, owned SHAKE cache and shared
SHA-512 cache. `compile_bind` and `compile_resume` preserve the ledger and
cache across composition/suspension. `read_snapshot` retains the actual
pre-read cumulative hash-log checkpoint through every supported continuation,
even after monitor failure. `actual_helper_snapshot` combines that guarantee
with actual-parent compatibility after partial seed reads.

These are structural and operational guarantees. An initial parent table is
not evidence of authenticated lineage; use an empty ledger or prove it arose
from the same instrumented prelude as the caches/checkpoints. Whole native
root/exposure coverage remains open, including explicit orphan and
receipt-linked exceptions, causal parent selection and trusted context/shape
interpretation. Late discovery is not retroactive security coverage. The
first-original-slot registry map, ordered-prefix grouping, native protocol
composition, attacker-work coupling, rectangular/numerical certification,
BabyBear and fail-closed Rust/scheduler refinement remain mandatory.

## Reconstructed parent state and declared-helper coverage

`NativeParentHistory` reconstructs the complete final ledger and owned SHAKE
cache from the ordered native observations. `compile_records` holds on every
supported free compiled execution, and `simulated_records` transports it
through any typed shared handler. Cache writes retain every returned byte,
including repeats and overlaps. Parent entries and frozen keys are monotone
under arbitrary later observations; splitting the history preserves the same
state by `record_append`.

`NativeParentStateExecution` extends reconstruction to the actual shared
checkpoint handler. The observation fold records newly resolved keys at the
pre-read hash log, advances the owned byte cache with the returned interval,
and updates the common SHA-512 cache/log and passive monitor at real hash
calls. `execute_records_support` proves this full-state invariant for every
supported execution. `execute_records` identifies the entire instrumented
computation with deterministic reconstruction from the original native
value/log computation. No additional coins or ghost-state input to native
continuations are introduced.

`state_law` and `from_empty` give exact conditional/unconditional event
probabilities including ledger, caches, checkpoints and monitor. `prefix_law`
also retains the actual residual native program; `execute_bind` threads every
field across composition. `after_prelude_law` derives all initial fields by
replaying the **same** complete prior log from empty initialization. Its
observed SHAKE cache and canonical shared hash cache are proved equal to the
caches required by the existing posterior law, removing separately supplied
initial ledger/checkpoint certificates for this case.

The `Covered` invariant means that every frozen context/root key has an
actual retained checkpoint. `record_covered`, `fold_covered` and
`execute_covered` preserve it, with `empty_covered` discharging initialization.
This certifies registration, not Merkle availability. `resolved_snapshot`
handles both cases: an already frozen key retains its earlier snapshot; a
newly resolved key is recorded at the current actual pre-read cumulative
hash log. Monitor failure does not prevent retention.

`NativeParentCoverage` now derives pending-parent membership from an earlier
observed input rather than assuming a parent-table entry. Any recognized
parent request observed in a start, raw read (including an empty read), or
shared hash declares its helper contexts. `binding_helper` obtains a context
from the exact canonical bind payload in those decoded frames. Later raw
activity preserves that declaration. With a truthful whole history and the
actual logical 64-byte parent seed quoted by the child, the helper root is
resolved using the history-owned cache even after partial seed reads.
`declared_helper_snapshot` consequently proves a retained checkpoint through
every supported continuation of a later nonempty child read, starting with
all fields reconstructed from the same prelude.

`prior_quote_target` and `prior_quote_event` connect earlier positive-read or
hash child-header candidates to the existing causally selected first-seed
exposure event. Its exact conditional probability remains the previously
proved prior-candidate count divided by `2^512` when **all** logical seed
coordinates were unobserved. This is not yet exhaustive orphan classification
or a lifetime union/work bound, and it gives no 512-bit claim for receipt
inputs or partially exposed seeds.

Next, prove exhaustive chronological root/exposure coverage for the actual
native schedule, including descendant and receipt-linked exceptions, then
compose availability and arithmetic with the actual attacker-work machine.
Trusted context/shape identity, first-original registry aliases, ordered-prefix
grouping, rectangular/numerical certification, BabyBear, application security
and fail-closed Rust/scheduler refinement remain open.

## Lifetime seed risk and inherited helper-context chains

`CausalExposureLifetime` accumulates the existing causally selected
first-seed-exposure risk over every finite analysis prefix of an unbounded
machine. Its local state is initialized from the actual prelude result, and
every prefix retains that prelude's entire raw log. Earlier child-header
candidates therefore remain in the target set. `lifetime_le_totalCharge`
bounds the union of an inherited bad event and all new exposure events by
the inherited event probability plus the expected sum of the per-step risks.
The nonnegative sum and integral may be infinite. No termination, finite mean,
query cap, discarded rejection path or success floor is assumed. This is a
**probability-risk charge**, not attacker work.

The conditional version retains the prelude result and log boundary as
proof-only data. `retained_history` projects it back to the original history;
it issues no oracle observation. `retained_replay` and `retained_event`
justify its full-history posterior, then `conditional_step_event` composes
that posterior inside the original prelude fiber. `conditional_lifetime_le`
preserves inherited bad probability and averages the same infinite risk sum
inside that fiber. Both the lifetime event and total charge are measurable.
The all-unobserved 64-byte seed premise remains exactly the earlier
first-read predicate; partial seeds and receipt guesses do not receive a
new 512-bit bound.

`NativeParentLineage.Known` is a finite chronological certificate made of
observed native parent requests. It starts with a directly parsed helper
context, follows actual logical seed quotes into later recognized parent
requests, and permits arbitrary intervening raw observations. It has no fixed
ancestry-depth limit. `Known.sound` proves that every such context occurs in
the actual table reconstructed from the same truthful history. The inherited
step uses every compatible old parent and the history-owned partial byte
cache, rather than requiring full seeds or selecting the first seed match.

`resolve_known_helper` extends helper-root resolution to those inherited
contexts. `known_helper_snapshot` consequently proves a retained checkpoint
through every supported continuation of a later positive-length raw read,
with ledger, byte cache, hash cache and checkpoints replayed from the same
empty initialization. A context need not occur directly in the descendant's
own frames. This does not backdate a snapshot for an earlier orphan read,
authenticate native ownership, or establish Merkle availability. Registration
through all compatible partial parents also does not yet supply a
single-context arithmetic loss; partial-seed association/collision accounting
remains part of the global Fiat–Shamir argument.

The next global obligation is to classify every security-relevant native
root/challenge exposure using chronological coverage or an explicit exception,
including inherited source keys and receipt-linked inputs. The risk charge
must then be coupled to an actual attacker-work machine, with prior work and
failure/abort paths retained. Native registry aliases/grouping, trusted
context/shape identity, rectangular/numerical certification, BabyBear,
application soundness/extraction and fail-closed Rust/scheduler refinement
remain required.

## Inherited source keys and causal seed-prequery coverage

`NativeSourceLineage` extends chronological metadata inheritance to complete
source `(context digest,root)` keys. Its `Known` certificate starts with a
source key parsed from an observed parent request, follows actual logical
seed quotes through later parent requests, and permits intervening raw

`firstRead_of_next_hit` excludes completed states, starts and shared hashes;
`selected_at_first_exposure` proves that the earliest seed hit in an actual
finite machine execution selects exactly the earlier prefix's pending read.
The proof uses actual suspension/resumption and ordered log prefixes, rather
than assuming that an input picked from a later witness was fixed earlier.

`prior_quote_lifetime` places an earlier matching child-header quote in the

are measurable without a measurable/countable attacker-state assumption;
their characterizations combine ordinary replayable prefix events and the
existing first-exposure event. The probability bounds transfer to the same
expected lifetime risk charge, with unconditional and prelude-conditional
forms that keep inherited bad probability. No input-space factor is added to
the loss: the actual pending request selects the input for the bound.

These events concern prior raw observations and an entirely unobserved
logical 64-byte seed. They do not classify a quote appearing for the first
time in the pending input, partial-seed association/collision cases, or
receipt-linked guesses. Exhaustive accepted-verifier coverage must still

## Pending seed quotes and derived native ancestry

`PendingSeedQuote` covers a seed quote first appearing in the currently pending
input. Its exact conditional guessing risk is 1/2^512 when all 64 logical seed
bytes remain unseen. This risk combines with earlier quoted-seed risks over an
unbounded execution, retaining prelude and inherited bad events.

`SeedQuoteOrder` proves that outside these two events, every observed input
quoting a producer's seed occurs strictly after that producer's first logical
seed exposure. This includes positive reads outside the seed window and shared
hash calls. Any finite closed dependency graph therefore implies a bad event.

`NativeSeedAncestry` starts from semantic source/helper ancestry and actual
producer-read occurrences, without assuming chronological parent order. It
derives chronological metadata, concrete root resolution before descendant
reads, and retained snapshots in the reconstructed shared oracle state. The
regressions include a distinct-output execution with a partial producer read,
an intervening shared hash, and a descendant read outside its seed window;
the absence of both bad events is proved for every execution prefix.

The two new smoke modules contain 20 examples and 35 guarded public-theorem
axiom reports. These results do not yet establish native accepted-run ancestry,
Merkle availability, partial-seed or receipt risk bounds, arithmetic soundness,
physical attacker-work coupling, or Rust/scheduler refinement. Probability
charges in these lemmas are not a physical-work accounting model.

## Native fork execution and program-machine bridge

`OracleProgramMachine` interprets each native program constructor as the
corresponding causal machine command. Its finite prefixes equal the existing
native program-prefix semantics exactly, including the retained continuation.
Every finite native program execution has a path-dependent completed prefix,
and every shorter machine log is a prefix of that same full native log. This
introduces no uniform retry bound, native cutoff, or physical-work model.

`NativeForkAncestry` obtains the producer seed read from execution of the actual
native fork. Canonical source keys and the helper context survive the shared
lookup's grouped/flattened multiplicity frames and are realized by its actual
initializer. Header preservation through the typed zero-count identity includes
its real receipt frame. Subsequent executed forks inherit source/helper facts
from that header without supplied seed-link equalities or producer-read indices.
The exact program-machine bridge transfers the existing risk-conditioned
chronology theorem to the full native program log.

The new regression uses a native parent with a canonical binding, a raw
prequery, shared lookup initialization, a nested fork and a final challenge.
It checks both equal-root/different-context source keys, helper ancestry,
retention of the raw query, metadata/root resolution before the final read,
and retained checkpoints through supported continuations. Reader starts alone
cannot realize a producer. Sixteen regression examples and twenty guarded
public-theorem axiom reports cover these additions.

The chronology/resolution/snapshot assertions retain the explicit absence of
prior/pending seed-quote bad events. Accepted native application runs still
need exhaustive certificate coverage and byte/domain validation. Merkle
availability, partial-seed and receipt risks, native stage admissibility,
full arithmetic/PCS composition, numerical certification for both fields,

## Causal PCS and ordered helper verification

`CausalHashWorkerPool` executes the original raw hash workers inside
`OracleProgram`. Scheduler selection is itself a mixed-oracle program, so
scheduler SHAKE/hash prequeries and worker authentication calls belong to the
same causal history. An accepted pool replays every original worker in the
common final hash cache, including when earlier and later work surround it.
Increasing worker analysis fuel extends the history; it does not impose a
native retry cap. Cancellation preserves the selected scheduler memory and
the complete observed prefix. This is an execution model; physical cost,
fairness, termination and native Rayon refinement remain open.

`NativeGoldPcsProgram` combines the actual native checked PCS prefix, that
worker pool and the existing computed suffix/claim check. The SHAKE reader
is no longer an external functional argument at this entry point. A completed
result derives its preparation, pool result, status and complete history
from the actual program execution. Accepted results enforce the original
claim fold and authenticate every original raw column/path, together with
both coordinate checks, in any truthful enclosing history containing the
actual run. No prepared-prefix or authentication certificate is supplied.
Because the whole execution is an `OracleProgram`, the existing shared lazy
SHAKE/hash interpreters and causal machine translation apply to it.

`NativeGoldHelperVerification.program` runs the actual parent/lookup/equality/
scalar/finish handoff and then verifies its computed helper calls in native
order. Each accepted call advances the transcript and scheduler memory and
records its computed result. The first nonaccepted call stops the loop,
retaining the last accepted progress and the complete failed or suspended
PCS outcome. A derived trace identifies precisely the passed prefix and the
first unpassed call. On completion, receipt order equals the actual helper
plan and its length equals the original helper-root count, using upstream
geometry gates to discharge the literal zip's lengths. Every recorded
helper's raw authentication replays in the final cache of the entire combined
execution, including later helper observations. A `.helpers ... (.done ...)`
result means helper verification completed; it does not mean final source
verification or application acceptance.

The regressions reuse the existing native canonical PCS and false-claim
fixtures without changing their bytes. They check exact mixed-oracle logs,
acceptance, native claim rejection, worker suspension, cancellation and
ordered helper stopping. Synthetic interleavings check scheduler prequeries,
shared hash reuse and cancellation memory. These tests do not constitute a
new full native accepted PBS fixture.

Remaining obligations include grouped source `verify_many`, exact ordered
left-prefix matrix grouping modulo the native field, root/word availability,
global Fiat–Shamir risk accounting, physical-work coupling, both native
parameter profiles, strict adversarial decoding and Rust/Charon/Aeneas/NTT/
SIMD/Div64/scheduler refinement. The full false-PBS/extraction and 128-bit
expected-work theorems remain unproved. The new deterministic authentication
results do not discharge those probability or implementation obligations.

## Original source ownership and native batch binding

`NativeSourceRegistry` computes alias groups from the full original ordered
registry, using both the complete computed context digest and the root.
Each group selects its first original slot, before any unused-source filter.
The owner is at or before each aliased slot, has exactly the same key, is
idempotent and is minimal among original slots. Equal roots with different
contexts remain distinct. These are digest-key facts; parameter equality
still needs the separate context-collision argument. Tests deliberately
include a colliding context oracle to preserve that boundary.

The metadata-bearing initializer erases to the existing native registry
initializer with the same returned parent and complete oracle log. Successful
preparation recovers that metadata and its original registration observations.
`bound_metadata` and `helpers_metadata` derive the original parameter/context/
root correspondence from the actual completed lookup body or helper pipeline;
callers do not supply an alias map or a successful-registration certificate.
An existing native completed-body fixture exercises this derivation.

`NativeGoldQueryGroups` groups response rows by the exact ordered list of
left-prefix matrix pairs. Every matrix retains its width and all ordered
entries; equality compares Goldilocks entries modulo the base field. Group
representatives are first original queries. Suffix differences may share a
response; reordered left matrices do not share merely because another
algebraic summary agrees. Equality keys do not replace the original raw
query bytes. Native binding/shape gates must precede use of the total key
functions.

`NativeGoldBatchBinding` implements native `bind_many`: reject empty or
mismatched counts and invalid query/value/matrix dimensions before context

context/root/queries/values tuple under `mw batched row-code v1`. Returned
bindings retain precisely those checked queries and values for subsequent
response grouping. Serialization failure and rejected binding preserve their
actual observed prefixes. This is the binding prefix of `verify_many`;
shared random-test sampling, responses, ordered columns, worker authentication
and finishing every original claim are now executed by the following layer.
Source-claim/seal/dispatch and application-security composition remain open.

## Shared native batch PCS execution

`NativeGoldBatchOpening` supplies the original non-hiding batch wire shape:
one random-test response, one evaluation response per computed ordered prefix
group, and one set of raw columns with leaf-first paths. Its prefix readers
cover constructed messages; strict adversarial Rust decoding/resource
refinement remains open.

`NativeGoldBatchPrelude` preserves the native `verify_many` order: construct
trusted geometry, bind the checked batch, then check proof shape, then request
one shared random matrix. Proof-shape rejection retains the already-bound
parent and context observations. The group count comes from the checked
queries. Suspension retains the active field state and does not become a
native rejection or impose a retry cap.

`NativeGoldBatchColumns` computes structured weights from each first original
prefix representative in group order, binds the test and all evaluation
responses in one native frame, and issues one atomic schedule-5 request.
The complete quota-sized ordered draw list is retained separately from its
ascending distinct transport indices. Successful results derive their
actual completed prelude, computed groups, atomic request and count gates;
no sampled-index or successful-prefix certificate is supplied.

`NativeGoldBatchColumnWorker` authenticates the original raw column/path
once, then performs the shared random test and every grouped structured
check in native lane/coordinate order. Each grouped check is related to the
existing single-response semantic coordinate interface. It does not replace
raw hashing with field-projected hashing or authenticate each group again.
Native Rayon/compiler and physical-cost refinement remain open.

`NativeGoldBatchPcsProgram` composes that prefix with actual retained-code
response encoding, one causal worker per distinct column, and an ordered
finish loop over **every original query**, including prefix aliases. The
program computes acceptance from the actual residual workers and native
claim comparisons. Prepared root/width/query/value provenance, matching group

## Native shared-budget field and first-stream matrix laws

`BudgetedUniformSequence` models one candidate budget shared across all
coefficients. Rejection consumes a candidate without advancing the coefficient
index. It proves the exact successful tuple law as the actual completion mass
times the joint uniform law, its two-branch completion recurrence and
monotonicity. It does not replace the native global candidate budget with a
separate retry budget per coefficient.

`NativeFieldVectorValues` and `NativeFieldVectorProgram` give exact typed-value
and complete ordered-log projections of actual native execution, including
rejected chunks, accepted prefixes and resumption. Final receipt emission does
not change the completed collector state. `FreshShakeTail` handles the real
cache: arbitrary entries outside the unread tail remain, earlier installed
bytes do not affect later positions, and any entry inside the tail prevents
freshness. `NativeFieldVectorFresh` derives the interpreter's single-candidate
law from canonical masked bytes and uses the actual shared cache transitions.

`NativeFieldVectorLaw` transfers the compiled law to the posterior after a
replayable whole mixed SHA512/SHAKE history. Its finite law retains the computed
completion factor. Native completed events are increasing under actual
resumption; their union over all candidate prefixes is bounded by the joint
uniform event probability. No completion conditioning, success floor or native
attempt limit is imposed. `NativeFieldMatrixLaw` transports this law through a
lane-major finite bijection, keeping modulus, test rows and source rows
independent.

`NativeGoldBatchRandomLaw` derives the actual completed prime request, geometry
count and canonical raw-word conversion from checked native batch preparation.
Its sampler matrix equals `work.random` at native lane-major addresses, then
reindexes to exactly `NativeGoldBatchRectangularChecks.random` on the common
left-cell/source-lane rows. The conditional law and unbounded domination apply
to this same rectangular matrix.

`CausalStreamExposure` selects the actual next first positive read of a complete
input. A first read can occur at any offset. All earlier positive reads of that
input count, including partial/far-offset reads; starts, empty reads and SHA-512
observations do not expose SHAKE coordinates. Eligibility proves the whole
stream is absent from the observed cache. `NativeGoldBatchFirstReadLaw` supplies
the checked native rectangular matrix law at this causal first-read point,
without an external freshness certificate.

Regressions use modulus three to force a rejected first byte, retained partial
coefficients and byte chunks, correct resumed values and read offsets. They
check shared-budget recurrence values `9/16` and `27/32`, actual posterior laws
after a cached read of a different input, rejection of overlapping-cache
freshness, far-offset first exposure and earlier-partial-read exclusion. The
actual three-packing/four-code-width Goldilocks batch supplies its eighteen
coefficients and instantiates the first-read rectangular law. Generic canonical
sampler/matrix transport also typechecks at BabyBear's modulus and width six;
this does not establish native BabyBear Montgomery/PCS integration. Forty-six
new axiom guards use only the allowed three axioms or subsets.

Remaining production obligations include complete first-exposure coverage and
past-measurability of the source/phase metadata through orphan, pending,
partial-seed and receipt lineage; the response-bound ordered-column law and
full global risk composition; efficient public extraction and PBS application
soundness; native BabyBear integration; physical attacker-work and final
128-bit numerics; and strict decoder plus Rust/Charon/Aeneas/NTT/SIMD/Div64/
scheduler refinement.

The native Goldilocks batch column request now has an exact first-read posterior

The complete request input binds the raw test row and every raw group response.
Field-equal lazy word aliases therefore remain different committed responses.
Authentication columns and paths are later data and do not enter this nonce.

The native field completion bridge identifies the actual receipt-derived parent.
Receipt replay works when all 64 receipt coordinates are already known, including

The regression covers two 32-byte reads, rejects a single partial receipt as

Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

This closes a local column-law interface, not the final security theorem. The
law requires receipt knowledge and an actual first read of the complete bound

## Complete-stream chronological coverage and adaptive index charges

`CausalStreamCoverage` locates the first positive read anywhere in a complete

or selected by `CausalStreamExposure.firstRead` at an actual earlier prefix.

The native-program interpreter yields a path-dependent completion prefix after

uniform termination/trial bound. The first exposures need not follow the
verifier's later order of use.

`NativeIndexExposureRisk` selects requests and event predicates from the current
complete history and checks eligibility against the actual pending first read.
It retains the complete native result and ordered observation log, proves the
exact conditional and averaged charge, and sums those charges over every
analysis prefix of an unbounded machine. Invalid dimensions, repeated streams
and mismatched pending requests contribute no event or charge. A shared-check
charge has one witness miss bound with the original ordered quota; it does not
acquire a group or lane factor.

reads/hash/start observations, same-stream versus foreign cached reads,

`NativeFieldObservationScope` proves that every actual collector observation is

## Native field-to-column posterior composition

`NativeGoldBatchChallengeScope` proves that a parsed complete column nonce

replayable retained histories. `NativeGoldBatchFieldColumnLaw` retains the
entire original selecting history and the actual field collector result/log,
derives column freshness from the original pending first read and the input
separation theorem, and proves the exact conditional uniform law on each
retained fiber. Averaging those fibers gives an exact original-posterior
identity for every predicate depending on the collector state and the ordered
column vector. Incomplete outcomes keep their original mass. Prior partial
field and receipt queries are permitted; no complete receipt knowledge or
field-stream freshness certificate is required for this column law.

`NativeGoldBatchFieldColumnBound` applies that identity to a family of column
checks depending on all collected field values. Given a disagreement witness
for each reachable completed state in the original posterior, the probability
of all checks passing is bounded by one shared ordered-quota miss term.
Completion stability gives the same bound over all collector budgets, with
no retry, group, or lane factor and no completion normalization.

[7, 1, 7], two state-dependent checks, a single disagreeing column, a partially

output, offset and nonempty bytes. Starts, hashes and empty reads remain in
the prefix but do not count as exposure. Once recovered, that prefix is
unchanged by arbitrary suffixes; no seed-window or lifetime cap is used.

`NativeGoldBatchFirstFieldSource` uses this prefix to recover the earlier
selected common source log from a later history. The strict linked-column
parser supplies its exact canonical field input. If that stream has already
been exposed, recovery succeeds; the recovered source has all 64 checkpoint
snapshots and remains unchanged after suffixes or actual auxiliary collector
reads. The source is computed from the old selecting history and parsed data,
not a future native preparation or a later hash log.

`NativeGoldBatchRecoveredSourceAvailability` proves that actual later native
acceptance uses that recovered source for every authenticated payload and
native column equation, outside the existing global disagreement event. Its
column-history theorem derives the actual field phase from the parsed native
column input, preserves the source through all later verification queries,
and needs no future source-log witness or supplied checkpoint certificate.

`NativeGoldBatchWitnessedColumnBound` bounds the event that a completed state
both has a distance witness and passes every shared column check. Unlike the
older unconditional-witness lemma, it does not require every completed state
to have a false response. Unwitnessed and suspended states retain their full
original probability mass. Exact posterior refinement gives the single
ordered-quota miss bound, and completion stability extends it over all native
collector budgets without a retry, group or lane factor. Measurability of the
all-budget event is also proved.

Regressions exercise ignored starts/empty reads, a first field read at offset
999, retention of hashes and other-input reads in the recovered prefix,
arbitrary suffixes, and preservation under auxiliary collection. An actual
accepted native run uses the source recovered before an intervening hash in
its column history. The probability regression includes a completed correct
state with no disagreement witness, demonstrating that no unconditional
witness premise is needed, as well as a witnessed passing state. Eighteen
new axiom guards cover the production lemmas.

Next, instantiate the witnessed event with the concrete combined random and
structured response family and the recovered old-history source. Map accepted
false original claims into that event or the first-field proximity event,
then apply complete causal exposure coverage and lifetime averaging. The
registry/context binding, remaining seed/lookup lineage, independent public
extractor, PBS semantics, native BabyBear, physical attacker work, strict
implementation refinement and final 128-bit inequality remain open.

Validation: full `scripts/check` passed with 10,541 build jobs, including
the combined HasteBoots smoke module and all subsequent audits. Separate
warning-as-error checks passed for all four new production modules and both
regression/audit modules. All eighteen new theorem axiom guards passed using
only the three allowed axioms or subsets. No axioms, proof placeholders,
native decision proofs or proof-limit increases were introduced.


## Concrete native column family and causal lifetime charge

`NativeGoldBatchConcreteColumnFamily` instantiates the test family with a sum
of random rows and parsed structured group/lane pairs. Both branches use the
same recovered source word and one ordered column vector. Raw combinations
use the actual retained coefficient state or the ordered structured weights;
claimed responses are computed from all parsed raw test/group rows. All
claimed responses are proved coded. These definitions take fixed parameters,
parsed data and the selected source log, with no arbitrary response callback
or future prepared work. Test width and code packing width remain separate.

`NativeGoldBatchConcreteColumnBound` instantiates the all-budget witnessed
bound with this family. Its source is computed from the selecting history by
first-field prefix recovery. The winning event contains its own disagreement
witness and all shared checks; correct or suspended states are not normalized
away. The distance is min(code-distance-minus-radius, radius+1), and its miss
term is proved equal to the maximum of the two branch miss terms. No union
factor is introduced for choosing a branch or response test.

`NativeGoldBatchConcreteColumnExposure` derives selection from the actual
pending first positive read and complete linked-column parser, checks the
native label, positive ordered quota and fixed code domain, and computes the
source from the old history. It proves the local conditional inequality,
measurability, averaging and a lifetime inequality over all causal machine
prefixes and all collector budgets. The risk is zero for ineligible/repeated
inputs and when no earlier field source is recoverable. The latter case
remains covered separately by the early-receipt reduction; zero column risk
does not assert that the complete native security loss is zero there.

`NativeGoldBatchConcreteColumnWitness` lifts the actual accepted-native
near-branch false-claim witness and the recovered-matrix far-branch witness
into this sum family at the minimum distance used by the causal bound.
The near lift retains the false original claim and parsed group bound.

Regressions use six combined tests, three ordered draws [7,1,7] and two
transported columns in the native three-test/four-packing fixture. They check
coding, source recovery, the exact single miss term (31/32)^3 at radius zero,
the conditional bound, absence of an earlier field source, repeated far-offset
column reads, source preservation over arbitrary suffixes, and the full
unbounded lifetime theorem. Fourteen new axiom guards cover the production
lemmas. These are probability charges, not physical attacker-work costs.

Next, prove that every accepted native false claim outside the first-field
proximity and shared source exceptions enters this concrete checked event.
This still needs the exact parsed-request draw identity and transport of all
accepted random/group checks to the concrete family on the same recovered
source. Then combine first-field proximity, early receipts and causal exposure
coverage. Registry/context ownership, remaining seed/lookup lineage, independent
public extraction, PBS semantics, native BabyBear, physical-work accounting,
strict implementation refinement and the final 128-bit inequality remain open.

The current concrete selector uses the parsed positive quota, rather than
asserting that it equals an owned application's trusted quota. Its lifetime
inequality is valid for that broader event, but must be restricted through the
registry/context and parameter-profile reduction before calibrating a final
128-bit application loss. A fixed-code-domain check alone is not such a
trusted-parameter binding.

Validation: full `scripts/check` passed with 10,546 build jobs, including
the combined HasteBoots smoke module and all subsequent audits. Separate
warning-as-error checks passed for all four new production modules and both
regression/audit modules. All fourteen new theorem axiom guards passed using
only the three allowed axioms or subsets. No axioms, proof placeholders,
native decision proofs or proof-limit increases were introduced.
